scheme.name: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi
scheme.description: Direct income support scheme providing Rs 6,000 per year in three equal installments to small and marginal farmer families.
scheme.goals: Provide income support of Rs 6,000/year to all farmer families. Cover 14.5 crore farmer families across India.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 14.5 crore small and marginal farmer families

pib.headline: PM Kisan: Rs 6,000 reaches 8.89 crore farmers during COVID
pib.summary: During COVID lockdown, PM Kisan transferred Rs 2,000 first instalment directly to 8.89 crore farmer accounts.

pib.headline: PM Kisan: Rs 2 lakh crore disbursed to 11 crore farmers
pib.summary: PM Modi releases 12th instalment of PM-KISAN. Total disbursal crosses Rs 2 lakh crore benefiting over 11 crore farmers.

pib.headline: PM-KISAN empowers farmers through timely financial assistance
pib.summary: The release states that PM-KISAN had disbursed more than Rs. 2.42 lakh crore to over 11 crore farmers. It highlights direct bank transfers, support for women beneficiaries, and positive effects on farm investment and rural incomes.

pib.headline: Government reports PM-KISAN coverage and disbursement progress
pib.summary: The Ministry describes PM-KISAN as providing Rs. 6,000 annually to eligible landholding farmer families through three direct-transfer instalments. It reports that more than Rs. 2.60 lakh crore had been disbursed to over 11 crore farmers.

pib.headline: AI chatbot launched for PM-KISAN beneficiaries
pib.summary: The Ministry launched an AI chatbot integrated with the PM-KISAN grievance-management system. The chatbot provides multilingual assistance on application status, payments, eligibility, and other scheme-related queries.

pib.headline: 17th PM-KISAN instalment announced for Varanasi
pib.summary: The release announced that the Prime Minister would release the 17th PM-KISAN instalment on June 18, 2024. More than 9.26 crore farmers were expected to receive over Rs. 20,000 crore through direct transfers.

pib.headline: 17th PM-KISAN instalment released to farmers
pib.summary: The Prime Minister released the 17th instalment of PM-KISAN from Varanasi. The release transferred about Rs. 20,000 crore to farmers and also recognized more than 30,000 self-help groups trained as Krishi Sakhis.

pib.headline: PM-KISAN reaches over 11 crore farmers in 17 instalments
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that PM-KISAN had transferred more than Rs. 3.24 lakh crore to over 11 crore farmers across 17 instalments. It reaffirmed that the scheme provides Rs. 6,000 annually through direct bank transfers for agricultural needs.

pib.headline: 18th PM-KISAN instalment announced for October 5
pib.summary: The Ministry announced that the Prime Minister would release the 18th PM-KISAN instalment from Washim, Maharashtra. The release said the instalment would take cumulative scheme disbursement above Rs. 3.45 lakh crore and support more than 11 crore farmers.

pib.headline: 18th PM-KISAN instalment disbursed to farmers
pib.summary: The Prime Minister released the 18th PM-KISAN instalment in Washim, Maharashtra. About Rs. 20,000 crore was transferred to approximately 9.4 crore farmers through direct benefit transfer.

pib.headline: PM-KISAN saturation drives add eligible farmers
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that saturation campaigns had added more than one crore eligible farmers during the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra and over 25 lakh more within the first 100 days of the new government. It said 9.59 crore beneficiaries received the 18th instalment.
pib.figureUnit: eligible farmers added within the first 100 days

pib.headline: 19th PM-KISAN instalment announced for February 24
pib.summary: The Agriculture Minister briefed the media on the upcoming 19th PM-KISAN instalment. The release stated that more than Rs. 3.46 lakh crore had already been disbursed to over 11 crore farmer families through 18 instalments.

pib.headline: 19th PM-KISAN instalment reaches 9.8 crore farmers
pib.summary: The Prime Minister released the 19th PM-KISAN instalment from Bhagalpur, Bihar. More than 9.8 crore farmers, including 2.41 crore women farmers, received direct financial assistance exceeding Rs. 22,000 crore.

pib.headline: PM-KISAN recovery and verification measures reported
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that more than Rs. 3.68 lakh crore had been disbursed through 19 instalments and that mandatory land seeding, Aadhaar-based payments, and e-KYC were being used to verify beneficiaries. It also stated that Rs. 416 crore had been recovered from ineligible beneficiaries.
pib.figureUnit: Indian rupees recovered from ineligible beneficiaries

pib.headline: PM-KISAN beneficiary and fund-release details published
pib.summary: The Ministry published instalment-wise details showing that more than Rs. 3.69 lakh crore had been disbursed through 19 instalments. It also described technological safeguards, mandatory e-KYC and Aadhaar-linked payments, and recovery of funds paid to ineligible beneficiaries.

pib.headline: 20th PM-KISAN instalment scheduled for August 2
pib.summary: The Ministry announced preparations for the 20th PM-KISAN instalment, scheduled to be released from Varanasi on August 2. It said Rs. 20,500 crore would be transferred to approximately 9.7 crore farmers through direct benefit transfer.

pib.headline: 20th PM-KISAN instalment transferred to 9.7 crore farmers
pib.summary: The Prime Minister released the 20th PM-KISAN instalment from Varanasi. The release transferred Rs. 20,500 crore directly to more than 9.7 crore eligible farmer beneficiaries.

pib.headline: 21st PM-KISAN instalment prioritized for flood-affected states
pib.summary: The Agriculture Minister released the 21st PM-KISAN instalment for farmers in Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, and Uttarakhand affected by floods and landslides. More than Rs. 540 crore was transferred directly to over 27 lakh farmers in the three states.

pib.headline: 21st PM-KISAN instalment announced with cumulative transfers above Rs. 3.70 lakh crore
pib.summary: The Ministry announced that the Prime Minister would release the 21st PM-KISAN instalment on November 19, 2025. It reported cumulative direct transfers exceeding Rs. 3.70 lakh crore to more than 11 crore farmer families through 20 instalments and highlighted digital innovations such as Kisan-eMitra and farmer registries.

pib.headline: 21st Instalment of PM-KISAN: Direct Benefit Transfer of ₹18,000 crore to 9 crore farmers with focus on calamity-affected states
pib.summary: The 21st PM-KISAN instalment provides approximately ₹18,000 crore through Direct Benefit Transfer to nearly 9 crore farmers. The release highlights Aadhaar-based e-KYC, digital land records, the PM-KISAN portal, Kisan-eMitra and the PM-KISAN mobile app as tools supporting transparent delivery and farmer access.

pib.headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi releases the 21st instalment of PM-KISAN
pib.summary: The 21st instalment of PM-KISAN was released in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, providing approximately ₹18,000 crore in direct financial assistance to around 9 crore eligible farmers. The release states that more than ₹3.70 lakh crore had been disbursed to over 11 crore farmer families through the scheme’s first 20 instalments.

pib.headline: 21st Instalment of PM-KISAN
pib.summary: The backgrounder describes the 21st PM-KISAN instalment as a ₹18,000-crore Direct Benefit Transfer for approximately 9 crore farmers, with particular focus on calamity-affected states. It also notes that more than ₹3.70 lakh crore had been disbursed to over 11 crore farmer families since the scheme began.

pib.headline: PM-KISAN and PMFBY Benefits extended to farmers in Maharashtra; PMFBY covers 93.81 lakh applications in Maharashtra
pib.summary: The release reports that the 21st PM-KISAN instalment benefited more than 9.34 crore farmers nationwide, including 4,63,142 beneficiaries in Kolhapur district. It states that over ₹4.09 lakh crore had been disbursed through 21 instalments, including ₹1,993.66 crore released to farmers in Kolhapur district.

pib.headline: 22nd Instalment of PM-KISAN: Direct Benefit Transfer of over ₹18,640 crore to 9.32 crore farmers
pib.summary: The release states that more than ₹18,640 crore was transferred as the 22nd PM-KISAN instalment to over 9.32 crore farmers, including more than 2.15 crore women beneficiaries. The instalment was disbursed on March 13, 2026, from Guwahati, Assam, and total scheme disbursements had exceeded ₹4.27 lakh crore through 21 instalments.

pib.headline: 23rd Instalment of PM-KISAN: Direct Benefit Transfer of over ₹18,880 crore to 9.44 crore farmers
pib.summary: The 23rd PM-KISAN instalment transferred more than ₹18,880 crore in direct financial assistance to over 9.44 crore farmers, including 2.18 crore women farmers. The release says the instalment was disbursed on June 20, 2026, at Tarakeswar in Hooghly, West Bengal, and that cumulative disbursements had exceeded ₹4.46 lakh crore.

cag.finding: Audit found irregular disbursement of PM-KISAN benefits to ineligible persons, including government employees, income-tax payers and deceased beneficiaries, reflecting weaknesses in beneficiary validation and monitoring.
cag.parameter: Eligibility and accuracy of PM-KISAN beneficiary records and payments
cag.claimed: Benefits were intended only for eligible farmer families meeting the scheme's exclusion criteria.
cag.actual: Benefits were paid to multiple categories of ineligible beneficiaries, including government employees, income-tax payers and deceased persons.
cag.reportExcerpt: Scrutiny of the database of PM-KISAN revealed that 2,911 beneficiaries were found to be ineligible up to March 2023 due to various reasons (untraceable, not having land ownership, beneficiaries do not belong to State, retired or serving government employees, and other exclusion criteria). Out of 2,911 beneficiaries, 2,763 ineligible beneficiaries were extended the benefit amounting to Rs 4.18 crore, 127 beneficiaries did not receive any instalment and ineligibility of remaining 21 were revoked by the State Nodal Officer (SNO). Cross-check of the PM-KISAN database with the Human Resource Management System (HRMS) managed by the Finance Department, Government of Tripura revealed that 337 out of 2,44,072 beneficiaries were State Government employees (Group B and Group C).

cag.finding: Payments made to 2.75 lakh deceased farmers: Rs 270 crore transferred to accounts of farmers who had already died, indicating lack of database maintenance.
cag.parameter: Dead farmer payments
cag.actual: Rs 270 crore to 2.75 lakh deceased

cag.finding: Audit identified irregular payment of PM-KISAN benefits to the same beneficiaries through the same bank accounts, indicating duplicate or inadequately controlled disbursements.
cag.parameter: Uniqueness and validity of beneficiary-bank-account payments
cag.claimed: Benefits were intended for eligible farmer families, with one family receiving the prescribed benefit.
cag.actual: Payments were recorded for the same beneficiaries using the same bank accounts.
cag.reportExcerpt: The report stated that these deficiencies resulted in the extension of scheme benefits to ineligible beneficiaries such as disbursement to both husband and wife, double payment to the same beneficiaries and transfer of benefits to multiple beneficiaries with the same bank account.

cag.finding: Improper identification, non-verification and weak monitoring resulted in PM-KISAN benefits being paid to ineligible recipients, including State Government pensioners; other ineligible payments were not adequately recovered.
cag.parameter: Value of PM-KISAN payments made to ineligible beneficiaries
cag.claimed: The scheme was intended to provide ₹6,000 per year in three instalments only to eligible farmer families.
cag.actual: ₹131.40 lakh was disbursed to State Government pensioners; recovery of payments to other ineligible beneficiaries was also deficient.
cag.reportExcerpt: Due to improper identification, non-verification and lapses in monitoring of PM-KISAN scheme, benefits amounting to ` 131.40 lakh were disbursed to State Government Pensioners. Besides, there were non-recovery of amount disbursed to Income Tax payees and ineligible beneficiaries, benefits extended to more than one family member, benefits extended to beneficiaries who do not own agriculture land, benefits extended to the deceased beneficiaries, non-receipt of administrative expenses amounting ` 420.38 lakh, benefits released to the beneficiaries pending for Physical Verification, non-setting up of Project Monitoring Unit and non-achieving of target of physical verification.

cag.finding: The subject-specific compliance audit found deficiencies in the implementation of PM-KISAN in Manipur, particularly in beneficiary identification, verification and payment controls.
cag.parameter: Compliance of PM-KISAN beneficiary identification, verification and disbursement processes
cag.claimed: The scheme was intended to transfer benefits only to verified farmer families owning cultivable land.
cag.actual: Audit identified shortcomings in implementation and compliance controls.
cag.reportExcerpt: There were delays in processing of application forms of beneficiaries by two to 16 months. Records of the beneficiaries were not properly maintained in the selected districts.

cag.finding: The PM-KISAN implementation in Assam was affected by large-scale ineligible applications, weak monitoring, fake or multiple registrations and very limited recovery of funds paid to non-entitled beneficiaries.
cag.parameter: Recovery of PM-KISAN funds released to non-entitled beneficiaries
cag.actual: Only 0.24 percent of funds released to non-entitled beneficiaries had been recovered; approximately 35 percent of applicants were reported as ineligible.
cag.reportExcerpt: Subsequently, the State Government declared that 11,72,685 (37 per cent) out of the 31,20,430 beneficiaries were ineligible through an inquiry conducted from May-July 2020 across the state. A mere 0.24 per cent of the funds released to these ineligible beneficiaries were received back till October 2021, which was not refunded to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

verdict.name: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 3 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
scheme.description: National programme to address the declining Child Sex Ratio and promote the welfare of girl children. Launched in Panipat, Haryana.
scheme.goals: Prevent gender-biased sex selective elimination. Ensure survival and protection of the girl child. Ensure education and participation of the girl child.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 100 districts with lowest Child Sex Ratios across India

pib.headline: BBBP: 100 districts covered, girl child enrolment up
pib.summary: On International Women Day, PM announces BBBP expansion. Female school enrolment in target districts up by 5.4%.

pib.headline: Child Sex Ratio improves by 16 points under BBBP
pib.summary: Ministry of Women & Child Development reports Child Sex Ratio at birth improved from 918 to 934 in BBBP districts, attributing success to the programme.

pib.headline: Review of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Scheme
pib.summary: A NITI Aayog evaluation found that the scheme generated significant mass mobilization against gender discrimination and developed community-level initiatives. The release also reported an improving national Sex Ratio at Birth from 918 in 2014-15 to 934 in 2019-20.
pib.figureUnit: percentage points improvement in national Sex Ratio at Birth

pib.headline: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme reports improved Sex Ratio at Birth
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that BBBP combines a nationwide advocacy campaign with multisectoral interventions in 405 districts. It cited an improvement in the national Sex Ratio at Birth from 918 in 2014-15 to 934 in 2019-20.
pib.figureUnit: percentage points improvement in national Sex Ratio at Birth

pib.headline: BBBP campaign covers 405 districts through multisectoral interventions
pib.summary: The Ministry described BBBP's objectives of preventing gender-biased sex selection, protecting girls, and promoting their education and participation. It stated that the scheme combines nationwide advocacy with multisectoral interventions in identified districts and does not provide direct benefit transfers.

pib.headline: Initiatives announced to address school dropouts among girls
pib.summary: The release said BBBP awareness campaigns are organized at district level to support the re-enrolment of girls who have dropped out at secondary level. It also highlighted recognition for meritorious students and complementary Samagra Shiksha measures such as enrolment drives, retention camps, and gender-sensitization activities.

pib.headline: BBBP reports gains in sex ratio, education and maternal-care indicators
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that BBBP advocacy helped increase national Sex Ratio at Birth from 918 in 2014-15 to 937 in 2020-21. It also cited higher secondary-school enrolment for girls, first-trimester antenatal registration, and institutional deliveries.
pib.figureUnit: percentage points improvement in national Sex Ratio at Birth

pib.headline: BBBP expanded nationwide under Mission Shakti
pib.summary: The Ministry stated that BBBP operates under the Sambal component of Mission Shakti and has been expanded to all districts through multisectoral interventions. Activities include promotion of sports, self-defence camps, girls' toilets, menstrual-hygiene facilities, awareness of the PC-PNDT Act, and girls' skilling.

pib.headline: Ministry announces 10th-anniversary BBBP celebrations
pib.summary: The Ministry announced a nationwide programme marking ten years of BBBP, with celebrations scheduled from January 22 to March 8, 2025. Planned activities included an oath-taking ceremony, a best-practices compendium, Mission Shakti and Mission Vatsalya portal launches, and local awareness events.

pib.headline: Ministry commemorates BBBP's 10th anniversary
pib.summary: The Ministry commemorated a decade of BBBP and described the scheme as having contributed to progress in gender equality and the status of girls. The inaugural event also launched a compendium of best practices, Mission Vatsalya and Mission Shakti portals, and the Mission Shakti mobile app.

pib.headline: Palamu launches 100-day BBBP awareness campaign
pib.summary: Palamu district in Jharkhand organized thematic awareness programmes under the 100 Din Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign to address gender inequality, education, health, safety, and child protection. The release reported more than 70 programmes and outreach to 1,999 beneficiaries through related thematic activities.

pib.headline: Haryana's Mahri Laado radio programme expands BBBP outreach
pib.summary: Haryana's Women and Child Development Department launched the Mahri Laado radio programme as a community-based BBBP initiative addressing gender inequality and promoting the value of daughters. Broadcasts on All India Radio combined stories, interviews, and discussions, with reported participation across seven districts.
pib.figureUnit: participants engaged across seven Haryana districts

pib.headline: BBBP expanded to all districts with measurable annual objectives
pib.summary: The Ministry said BBBP is fully funded by the Central Government and has been expanded to cover every district. It reported that national Sex Ratio at Birth rose from 918 in 2014-15 to 930 in 2023-24, alongside improvements in girls' secondary-school enrolment, institutional deliveries, and antenatal-care registration.
pib.figureUnit: percentage points improvement in national Sex Ratio at Birth

pib.headline: BBBP reports continued improvement in sex ratio and girls' enrolment
pib.summary: The Ministry described BBBP as a national movement focused on behavioural and social change toward the girl child. It reported that national Sex Ratio at Birth increased from 918 in 2014-15 to 929 in 2024-25, while girls' secondary-school gross enrolment rose from 75.51% to 80.2%.
pib.figureUnit: percentage points improvement in national Sex Ratio at Birth

pib.headline: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Scheme helps to address Child Sex Ratio and related issues of empowerment of girls and women
pib.summary: The scheme has expanded nationwide under Mission Shakti’s SAMBAL vertical through multisectoral interventions focused on behavioural and social change. The national Sex Ratio at Birth improved from 918 in 2014-15 to 929 in 2024-25, while girls’ secondary-level gross enrolment ratio rose to 83.4% in 2025-26.

cag.finding: Haryana did not fully achieve the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao targets for improving the sex ratio at birth, increasing girls' enrolment in secondary education, and re-enrolling 100 percent of girls who had dropped out.
cag.parameter: Sex ratio at birth, girls' secondary-school enrolment, and re-enrolment of dropout girls
cag.claimed: Improvement in the sex ratio at birth, increased secondary-school enrolment of girls, and 100 percent re-enrolment of dropout girls
cag.actual: The targets were not fully achieved
cag.reportExcerpt: Targets of 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' of improving the sex ratio at birth, increasing girl’s enrollment in secondary education and 100 per cent re-enrolment of drop-out girls could not be fully achieved.

cag.finding: The report’s table of funds directly transferred to State Implementing Agencies records ₹44.95 lakh released through one NGO for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao under the Social Welfare Department.

cag.actual: ₹44.95 lakh released through one NGO for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao

cag.finding: The audit included a dedicated compliance audit of the implementation of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Scheme in Uttarakhand and reported deficiencies in implementation.
cag.parameter: Implementation of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Scheme
cag.actual: Deficiencies were identified in implementation
cag.reportExcerpt: The number of paragraphs this year is 17 including 11 theme based compliance audit paragraphs viz., ‘Enforcement of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006’, ‘Prevention of forest fires’, ‘Setting up of Private Universities’, ‘Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States’, ‘Recovery of Loans and Government Dues by District Collectors’, ‘108 Emergency Response Service’, ‘Post Matric Scholarship to the students belonging to SC and OBC’, ‘Infrastructure Development for Tourist Destinations and Circuits’, ‘Setting up of projects of Sewage Treatment Plants under Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission’, ‘Implementation of the Nirbhaya Scheme’ and ‘Implementation of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Scheme’.

scheme.name: Jal Jeevan Mission
scheme.description: Mission to provide safe and adequate drinking water through tap connections to all rural households by 2024. Renamed from NRDWP.
scheme.goals: Provide Har Ghar Jal (tap water to every household). Connect 19.26 crore rural households with tap water by 2024.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 19.26 crore rural households

pib.headline: Jal Jeevan: 3 crore connections in 16 months, Rs 50,000 crore spent
pib.summary: Ministry of Jal Shakti announces 3 crore rural households received tap water connections in 16 months under Jal Jeevan Mission.

pib.summary: The government reported that about 12.30 crore additional rural households had received tap-water connections under Jal Jeevan Mission by March 17, 2025. More than 15.53 crore households, or 80.20 percent of rural households, were reported to have tap-water supply at home.

pib.summary: The Ministry described the monitoring and assessment activities used to verify household tap-water coverage and functionality under Jal Jeevan Mission. The release emphasized state-level reporting, field verification and assessment of whether connections provide regular and quality-compliant water.

pib.headline: Jal Jeevan Mission targets extension through 2028
pib.summary: The government said the mission's proposed extension through 2028 would focus on completing remaining works and improving infrastructure quality and operations and maintenance. The extended approach would emphasize community participation and sustainable, citizen-centric water delivery.
pib.figureUnit: target year for the proposed mission extension

pib.headline: Safe and pure water in rural areas
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that approximately 12.33 crore additional rural households had received tap-water connections by March 31, 2025. More than 15.56 crore households, or 80.38 percent of rural households, were reported to have tap-water supply at home.
pib.figureUnit: crore rural households with tap-water supply

pib.headline: Challenges under Jal Jeevan Mission
pib.summary: The government reported that approximately 12.43 crore additional rural households had been provided tap-water connections, taking total coverage above 15.67 crore households as of July 21, 2025. It identified water scarcity, contamination, difficult terrain, limited technical capacity and delays in clearances as major implementation challenges.
pib.figureUnit: crore rural households with tap-water supply

pib.summary: The Ministry reported that about 12.44 crore additional rural households had received tap-water connections by July 23, 2025. It said the government was actively considering extending Jal Jeevan Mission until 2028 with enhanced funding and a stronger focus on infrastructure quality and maintenance.

pib.headline: Fluoride-affected habitations decline under Jal Jeevan Mission
pib.summary: The Ministry reported a decline in fluoride-affected habitations from 7,996 in April 2019 to 248 as of July 23, 2025. It attributed the response to source diversification, piped-water schemes and interim community purification measures in affected areas.

pib.headline: Nal Se Jal Mission reaches 81 percent rural household coverage
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that around 12.45 crore additional rural households had received tap-water connections by August 18, 2025. Overall coverage was reported at approximately 15.69 crore households, or 81.02 percent of rural households, with more than 2.63 lakh villages classified as Har Ghar Jal.
pib.figureUnit: crore rural households with tap-water supply

pib.headline: Tap water to all rural households
pib.summary: The government reported that about 12.56 crore additional rural households had received tap-water connections by January 24, 2026. More than 15.79 crore households, representing 81.56 percent of rural households, were reported to have tap-water supply, while almost the entire approved central budget had been utilized.
pib.figureUnit: crore rural households with tap-water supply

pib.headline: Impact of Jal Jeevan Mission
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that more than 15.79 crore rural households had tap-water connections as of January 29, 2026, with 189 districts and 2,50,021 villages reported as Har Ghar Jal. pib.figureUnit: crore women-hours potentially saved per day

pib.headline: Implementation status of Jal Jeevan Mission
pib.summary: The government reported that more than 12.58 crore additional rural households had received tap-water connections by March 3, 2026. Overall household coverage stood at about 15.82 crore, or 81.71 percent, while an independent functionality assessment found that 76 percent of surveyed household connections were functional.
pib.figureUnit: percent of assessed household tap connections found functional

pib.summary: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation released the operational guidelines for Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 during the culmination of Jal Mahotsav 2026. The revised phase shifts emphasis from rapid infrastructure creation toward sustainability, functionality, accountability and long-term rural water service delivery through December 2028.
pib.figureUnit: end year of the extended JJM 2.0 period

cag.finding: Punjab reported achieving functional tap connections for 100 per cent of rural households, but CAG found inaccurate and unstructured Annual Action Plans, unrealistic targets, underutilisation of funds, inadequate sustainability measures, weak operation and maintenance arrangements, and insufficient water-quality monitoring.
cag.parameter: Functional Household Tap Connection coverage and scheme implementation
cag.claimed: 100 per cent rural household coverage by 5 April 2023
cag.actual: The reported achievement could not be reliably supported because planning data were inaccurate and key implementation and monitoring deficiencies persisted
cag.reportExcerpt: The implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) in Punjab encountered several structural and operational challenges. Annual Action Plans were inaccurate and unstructured, failing to account for households already having drinking water access. This led to underutilisation of funds, inability to meet utilisation thresholds and delays in Utilisation Certificates, hindering further release of Central Share. There was an absence of critical planning tools like the State Action Plan (SAP), resulting in unrealistic targets. Over-reliance on over-exploited groundwater with limited adoption of sustainability measures was noticed. Lack of a formal O&M strategy and inadequate handover of schemes to Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSC) was observed. Insufficient Block-Level Laboratories and shortage of trained human resources led to inadequate water quality monitoring. Punjab reported to have achieved the JJM target of providing functional tap connections to 100 per cent rural households by 5 April 2023.

cag.finding: In Chhattisgarh, deficiencies in planning, fund management, scheme execution and water-quality monitoring resulted in non-achievement of the Jal Jeevan Mission's primary output and intended outcomes.
cag.parameter: Achievement of programme output and outcome
cag.actual: The primary output and outcome targets were not achieved; CAG also found mismatched data, delayed or short fund transfers, excess payments and shortfalls in water-quality testing
cag.reportExcerpt: Chhattisgarh was lagging in achieving the target and even though achievement of FHTC was 78 per cent as of March 2024, the schemes were in progress and not yet completed. Hence, the programme objective i.e. key output of delivering drinking water at the doorstep of every rural HHs has not been fully achieved.

cag.finding: Water-supply schemes, including NRDWP/Jal Jeevan Mission components, faced inadequate planning and financial sustainability; water charges amounting to ₹278.20 crore were not recovered.
cag.parameter: Recovery of water charges
cag.actual: ₹278.20 crore remained unrecovered
cag.reportExcerpt: Non-recovery of water charges amounting ₹ 278.20 crore

cag.finding: In Maharashtra, tap connections from private or own sources were included in Jal Jeevan Mission coverage even though their functionality was not established. In six test-checked districts, 9.64 lakh such connections were included in the dashboard total.
cag.parameter: Reported tap-connection coverage under JJM
cag.claimed: 37.89 lakh tap connections shown on the JJM dashboard in six selected districts
cag.actual: 9.64 lakh connections were from private or own sources and could not be counted as verified JJM Functional Household Tap Connections
cag.reportExcerpt: At the State level, 27.74 lakh private tap connections were shown covered under JJM. In the selected six districts, JJM dashboard showed 37.89 lakh tap connections which included 9.64 lakh tap connection from private/own source which were yet to be covered under the JJM. cag.finding: In Chhattisgarh, against a projected demand of five lakh urban dwelling units under PMAY-Urban, only 2.07 lakh units had been completed as of April 2025; audit also noted delayed planning and substantial curtailment of sanctioned projects.
cag.parameter: Completion of dwelling units against projected demand
cag.claimed: Demand for five lakh dwelling units was projected in the approved Housing for All Plans of Action
cag.actual: 2.07 lakh dwelling units completed as of April 2025
cag.reportExcerpt: A total demand for 5 lakh Dwelling Units (DUs) was projected by the State Government in the approved Housing for All Plan of Action (HFAPOAs) prepared for 168 ULBs against which 2.49 lakh DUs (50 per cent of demand) were taken up for construction and 2.07 lakh DUs were completed as of  April 2025. We noticed that Housing for All Plan of Actions (HFAPOAs) were prepared and approved (April 2018 for 36 ULBs and February 2022 for 132 ULBs) by State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (SLSMC) with delay of three to six years of implementation of the scheme. Meanwhile, projects under AHP/BLC/ISSR verticals were sanctioned by the SLSMC and Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC) for construction of 1.48 lakh DUs without preparation of HFAPOAs, Annual Implementation Plan (AIP) and finalisation of beneficiaries list indicating deficient planning. Approval of projects without identification and validation of beneficiaries led to curtailment of projects later on. During the period of 2015-16 to 2023-24, out of total sanctioned 75,164 DUs in Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) vertical, 37,067 DUs (49 per cent) have been curtailed/surrendered. Out of remaining 38,097 DUs, only 23,242 DUs (61 per cent) were completed as of April 2025. Similarly, out of total sanctioned 2.77 lakh houses in BLC vertical, 66,383 houses (24 per cent) were surrendered/curtailed, and out of remaining 2.11 lakh houses, 1.84 lakh houses (87 per cent) were completed.

cag.finding: The Housing for All Plan of Action was completed only in March 2022 instead of June 2016. Of the 13.92 lakh houses identified for urban poor households, 6.84 lakh did not receive the intended benefits because the State failed to obtain sanctions in time. Further, 2.66 lakh sanctioned houses remained incomplete after the mission period.
cag.parameter: Coverage of identified urban housing demand under PMAY-U
cag.claimed: Tamil Nadu identified a demand for 13.92 lakh houses for urban poor households.
cag.actual: 6.84 lakh identified houses were deprived of intended benefits because they were not sanctioned.
cag.reportExcerpt: The Housing for All Plan of Action was completed only in March 2022 instead of June 2016. Of the 13.92 lakh houses identified for urban poor households, 6.84 lakh did not receive the intended benefits because the State failed to obtain sanctions in time. cag.finding: In Puducherry, although 44,315 beneficiaries were found eligible for the PMAY-Urban Beneficiary Led Construction component, benefits were provided to only 14,826, denying assistance to 29,489 eligible beneficiaries.
cag.parameter: Coverage of eligible beneficiaries
cag.claimed: 44,315 beneficiaries were eligible for the scheme
cag.actual: Only 14,826 eligible beneficiaries received scheme benefits
cag.reportExcerpt: Compliance Audit on Implementation of Beneficiary Led Construction component of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) – Urban by the UT of Puducherry revealed that even though 44,315 beneficiaries were found to be eligible for the scheme, the scheme was implemented only to 14,826 beneficiaries, thereby denying the scheme benefits to 29,489 beneficiaries.

cag.finding: In Karnataka, only 88,395 dwelling units were completed out of 517,531 approved units under the AHP and BLC components, leaving most approved houses incomplete and making the Housing for All by 2022 objective unlikely to be achieved.
cag.parameter: Completion of approved dwelling units
cag.actual: 88,395 of 517,531 approved dwelling units completed as of March 2021
cag.reportExcerpt: As of March 2021, under AHP and BLC verticals, projects were taken up only for 5,17,531 beneficiaries out of the 13,71,592 prospective beneficiaries (38 per cent) identified through demand survey. As against the approved 5,17,531 DUs, only 88,395 DUs (17 per cent) were completed as of March 2021. The construction of 3,28,499 DUs (63 per cent) were yet (March 2021) to be commenced indicating that achieving the mission goal of ‘Housing for All’ by 2022 was a difficult prospect.

cag.finding: In its district-centric audit of selected urban local bodies in Cuttack and Sambalpur districts, CAG reviewed implementation of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) and observed that the State had limited implementation to the beneficiary-led subsidy component, leaving other PMAY-U components unimplemented in the audited urban areas.
cag.parameter: Coverage and implementation of PMAY-U components in audited urban local bodies

cag.finding: The Jharkhand audit found that the SBM(U)-supported municipal solid-waste system was not fully streamlined, with deficiencies across planning, financing, IEC, segregation, collection, transportation, processing and final disposal.
cag.parameter: End-to-end municipal solid-waste management in sampled ULBs
cag.actual: Audit test-checked 14 ULBs and found inadequate planning and institutional mechanisms, weak utilisation and monitoring of SWM funds, ineffective IEC activities, incomplete segregation and processing arrangements, and continued unsanitary disposal.
cag.reportExcerpt: Under the Mission, the Urban Development and Housing Department (the Department), Government of Jharkhand (GoJ), was required to streamline and formalise Solid Waste Management (SWM) systems, through a systematic process, comprising of (i) waste segregation and storage at source (ii) primary collection (iii) secondary storage (iv) transportation (v) secondary segregation (vi) resource recovery (vii) processing and (viii) treatment and final disposal of the solid waste. Audit, however, noticed that the Solid Waste Management Plan (short and long term) were not being prepared, by any of the 14 test-checked ULBs.

cag.finding: The audit of solid waste management in Meghalaya identified weak institutional planning, inadequate achievement of service-level benchmarks, deficiencies in financial management, and continued open dumping.
cag.parameter: Urban solid-waste planning, service delivery and scientific disposal under SBM(U)-aligned requirements
cag.actual: ULBs and state authorities had gaps in SWM plans, contingency planning, waste-generation assessment, informal-sector integration, segregation, processing and disposal, including open dumping.
cag.reportExcerpt: Based on the analysis in the preceding paragraphs, Audit concludes that the function of Municipal Waste Management in the state of Meghalaya is severely hampered due to weak institutional mechanism that is manifested in none of the multiple agencies involved in this process being compliant with the responsibilities assigned to them under the Meghalaya SWM Rules. Waste Management Plans (either short term or long term) were not prepared in the test checked ULBs/Town Committee except for Shillong Municipal Area, where a City Solid Waste Action Plan had been prepared by the Shillong Municipal Board (SMB) but the same was still awaiting approval. These delays in preparation and approval of requisite legislations and plans had inhibited the implementation of SWM activities. Analysis of financial resources for the solid waste management in Meghalaya has brought out that over a period of previous five years, bulk of the financial resource Performance Audit on Solid Waste Management in Urban Areas of Meghalaya has been received under the Asian Development Bank’s external funded project of NERCCDIP. During the period from 2017-18 to 2021-22 in Meghalaya, the State Government heavily relied on external funding from Asian Development Bank and Central grants, while the budgetary support from the State budget as agencies’ own resources contributed only a minor share towards financing of Solid Waste Management activities. Test check of urban agglomerations revealed that significant portion (70 per cent to 98 per cent) of municipal waste ended up in landfills without any processing.

cag.finding: The Uttar Pradesh audit found delayed and inadequate release and utilisation of SBM(U) funds, weak planning and capacity building, and poor performance in segregation, processing and scientific disposal.
cag.parameter: Release and utilisation of SBM(U) funds and achievement of urban solid-waste-management outcomes
cag.claimed: Funds were to be released to ULBs under the SWM, capacity-building and IEC components in accordance with SBM(U) plans.
cag.actual: During 2016-22, the share of available SWM funds released to ULBs ranged from 0 to 63 percent; release under capacity building and administrative expenses ranged from 0 to 20 percent, while IEC and public-awareness releases ranged from 3 to 62 percent. Test-checked ULBs also had substantial unutilised balances and delays in State-level fund release.
cag.reportExcerpt: Further, SWM plan was prepared in only three out of 45 test-checked Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). SWM related bye-laws were framed in only 12 ULBs out of 45 test-checked ULBs. The bye-laws framed by these ULBs lacked uniformity. Against proposed 112 training programmes for capacity building of human resources in ULBs, only 53 training programs were organised due to delay in administrative approval by the State Government and inadequate funding. During 2016-22, percentage of fund released to ULBs vis-a-vis available fund under SWM component ranged between zero and 63 per cent. Further, this percentage was zero to 20 per cent and three to 62 per cent respectively in Capacity Building and Administrative & Office Expenses (CB & AOE) and IEC&PA components, leaving a substantial unutilised balance during all years of the audit period at the level of State Mission Director (SMD), Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) (Urban). Moreover, State Government had released funds to the SMD with a delay ranging from 55 to 236 days and 11 to 1,098 days under SWM and CB & AOE respectively. Test-checked ULBs were collecting and transporting mixed waste to the plant, landfill or dumpsite. No instances of source segregation were found during the public survey of households in the test-checked ULBs. At the State level between 26 to 71 per cent of waste was processed during the year 2016-22 out of the total waste collected and at the ULBs level, between zero to 63 per cent waste was processed during the year 2016-22. Operation and maintenance of solid waste processing plants were found deficient in test-checked ULBs. Quantity of legacy waste had increased due to lack of proper disposal of waste in ULBs.

cag.finding: The Assam audit found that the State's draft urban solid-waste policy remained unapproved and that urban local bodies had significant deficiencies in planning, funding, processing and monitoring of waste-management activities.
cag.parameter: State policy, funding and operational performance of urban solid-waste management
cag.actual: The draft Assam Urban SWM Policy, 2018 was still unapproved by March 2023; audit also identified deficiencies in fund position, human resources, waste management and monitoring, including problems with SBM(U)-funded organic-waste composting facilities.
cag.reportExcerpt: The “Draft Assam Urban Solid Waste Management (SWM) Policy, 2018” was yet to be approved by the Government till March 2023 even after three years of submission by Director of Municipal Administration (DMA) and six years after notification of the SWM Rules, 2016.

cag.finding: Only 22 per cent of funds were utilised by urban local bodies, resulting in delays in implementing solid waste management projects under Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban).
cag.parameter: Utilisation of funds for SBM (Urban) solid waste management projects
cag.actual: 22 per cent of funds utilised
cag.reportExcerpt: As of March 2020, SLHPC approved DPRs worth Rs 863.8 crore for implementation of SWM in selected 18 ULBs, of which Rs 249.7 crore was received from central and state government. However due to delay in approval of DPRs, overall utilization had been meagre Rs 54.61 crore (22%). It is thus highly unlikely that SWM projects approved by SLHPC would be completed by the end of the Mission period (March 2021).

cag.finding: The performance audit of SBM in Arunachal Pradesh found deficiencies in implementation of the urban component, including failure to prepare project reports or DPRs for public and community toilets.
cag.parameter: Planning and implementation of SBM(U) sanitation infrastructure
cag.actual: The Mission Director had not prepared project reports or DPRs for construction of public/community toilets; audit noted that universal access, ergonomic design and lower operation and maintenance costs could not therefore be assured.

cag.finding: The audit found deficiencies in planning, institutional arrangements, fund utilisation, segregation, collection, processing and scientific disposal of municipal solid waste in urban local bodies.
cag.parameter: Effectiveness and scientific management of municipal solid waste in urban local bodies
cag.actual: Urban local bodies had not fully established effective systems for waste assessment, segregation, collection, processing and disposal; audit also identified gaps in SBM-related planning and fund utilisation.
cag.reportExcerpt: We observed that until the preparation of DPRs, none of the test-checked ULBs assessed the requirement of capital and revenue funds for SWM activities and hence, they were unaware of the resource deficit. Based on JPVs, we found that segregation at source was not followed in 32 out of 35 test-checked ULBs and it was partially carried out in three test-checked ULBs (CC, Tumakuru, CMC, Dandeli and TMC, Kumta). As evident from above, 92 per cent of the waste was collected and only 26 per cent was processed each year and a major portion of the remaining MSW was dumped at landfills, which would have a harmful impact on health and environment.

cag.finding: Eleven urban local bodies did not receive the Central share of SBM-Urban funds because DPRs were not prepared and submitted on time.
cag.parameter: Receipt of Central SBM-Urban funding by ULBs
cag.actual: Eleven ULBs did not receive Central assistance amounting to ₹45.82 crore.
cag.reportExcerpt: Eleven ULBs did not receive Central share worth ₹45.82 crore, due to non-preparation and timely submission of DPRs.

cag.finding: The Uttarakhand audit found that urban local bodies had not established effective systems for waste planning, collection, transportation, processing and sanitary disposal.
cag.parameter: Implementation of solid-waste management systems in urban local bodies
cag.actual: Deficiencies included ineffective baseline waste analysis, incomplete or defective DPRs, non-use of personal protective equipment, lack of systems for integrating informal waste workers, roadside dumping, open dumping due to unavailable sanitary landfill sites, and uncovered transport vehicles.
cag.reportExcerpt: The State Government needs to devise systems to assist ULBs in preparation of Solid Waste Management plans/action plans for effective implementation of waste management and monitor their effective implementation.

cag.finding: The audit found major deficiencies in implementation of Individual Household Latrines and public toilets; only 10 per cent of constructed Individual Household Latrines were functional.
cag.parameter: Functionality of Individual Household Latrines constructed under SBM (Urban)
cag.actual: Only 10 per cent of constructed latrines were functional
cag.reportExcerpt: Only 10 per cent of the IHHLs constructed were found functional.

cag.finding: An SBM (Urban) solid waste management project of Lumding Municipal Board remained unfruitful despite fund availability; inadequate follow-up and payment of an unsecured advance led to unfruitful expenditure of ₹30.51 lakh.
cag.parameter: Completion and productive utilisation of the solid waste management project
cag.actual: ₹30.51 lakh incurred as unfruitful expenditure
cag.reportExcerpt: 8.4.4 Unfruitful expenditure on Solid Waste Management project under Lumding Municipal Board remained unfruitful for years despite availability of funds under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban. Lack of active pursuance compounded by payment of unsecured advance to the project contractor by the Lumding Municipal Board, resulted in an expenditure of ₹30.51 lakh remaining unfruitful.

cag.finding: The Government stated that grants received from the Ministry for Swachh Bharat Mission Urban Phase-I during 2014-2022 were ₹61.99 crore, while ₹85.30 crore was allocated for Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0.
cag.parameter: SBM Urban funding
cag.claimed: ₹61.99 crore received under SBM Urban Phase-I during 2014-2022
cag.actual: ₹85.30 crore allocated for SBM 2.0

cag.finding: Out of 18 test-checked ULBs, Detailed Project Reports were prepared by only six ULBs under ISWM/SBM 1.0 and 11 ULBs under SBM 2.0. In three test-checked ULBs where DPRs were prepared, the prescribed waste-generation assessment method was not followed.
cag.parameter: Detailed Project Reports and waste-generation assessment under SBM
cag.actual: DPRs prepared by 6 ULBs under ISWM/SBM 1.0 and 11 ULBs under SBM 2.0

cag.finding: In West Bengal, 13,709 metric tonnes of solid waste was generated per day during 2021-22 and 13,687 tonnes per day was collected, but only 3,047 tonnes per day, or 22.26 per cent of collected waste, was treated; the remaining 10,640 tonnes per day was unscientifically disposed of.
cag.parameter: Solid waste collection and treatment
cag.actual: Only 3,047 TPD of 13,687 TPD collected waste was treated; 10,640 TPD was unscientifically disposed of.

cag.finding: Fourteen test-checked Urban Local Bodies in Telangana failed to fully utilise funds provided under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban, leaving 37 per cent of the allocated funds unspent as of March 2022.
cag.parameter: SBM-Urban fund utilisation
cag.actual: 37 per cent of allocated SBM-Urban funds remained unspent.

cag.finding: In Punjab during 2021-22, approximately 4,222 metric tonnes of solid waste was generated per day and 4,207 metric tonnes per day was collected, but only 1,471 metric tonnes per day was treated, leaving nearly two-thirds of collected waste untreated.
cag.parameter: Solid waste collection and treatment
cag.actual: Only 1,471 TPD of 4,207 TPD collected waste was treated.

verdict.name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 4 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: Namami Gange Programme
scheme.description: Integrated conservation mission to accomplish effective abatement of pollution, conservation and rejuvenation of the Ganga river.
scheme.goals: Reduce pollution in Ganga to acceptable limits by 2022. Nirmal Ganga (clean Ganga) by 2020. Aviral Ganga (continuous flow) throughout.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Population living along the Ganga basin; 5 main-stem states

pib.headline: Namami Gange: 152 STPs commissioned, treating 4,000 MLD sewage
pib.summary: National Mission for Clean Ganga announces 152 sewage treatment plants commissioned with 4,000 MLD treatment capacity along Ganga.

pib.headline: Namami Gange: Ganga declared cleanest in decades, Rs 30,000 crore spent
pib.summary: NMCG announces Ganga water quality has improved significantly. BOD levels within acceptable limits at 97% monitoring stations. 30,015 crore committed.

pib.headline: Cleaning and Conservation of Rivers
pib.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti stated that river cleaning and rejuvenation are continuous processes, with the Central Government supporting States and Union Territories through the Namami Gange Programme for the Ganga and its tributaries. The release also described sewage-treatment approaches, monitoring systems, and innovations such as the Hybrid Annuity Model and One City-One Operator concept.

pib.headline: A Holistic Approach for Cleanliness of River Ganga
pib.summary: The release describes Namami Gange as an integrated conservation mission focused on pollution abatement, conservation, and rejuvenation of the Ganga. It states that the programme was extended through March 2026 with a budgetary outlay of ₹22,500 crore and aims to improve sewage treatment, water quality, and industrial-waste regulation.

pib.headline: Restoring the divine Glory of River Ganga: Namami Gange Programme achieves significant milestones
pib.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti reported progress in pollution abatement, ecological restoration, capacity building, and community engagement under Namami Gange. It stated that the programme had created 3,446 MLD of sewage-treatment capacity and completed 127 projects and 152 sewage-treatment plants.

pib.headline: Namami Gange Mission 2.0: 7 major sewerage infrastructure projects completed in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Delhi in the 2nd half of FY 2024-25
pib.summary: Seven major sewerage-infrastructure projects were completed under Namami Gange Mission 2.0 in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Delhi during the second half of financial year 2024-25. Their commissioning raised the programme’s total sewage-treatment capacity to 3,722 MLD and the number of commissioned STPs to 157.

pib.headline: Unique Success of the Namami Gange Mission: The Return of the Red-Crowned Roofed Turtle to the Ganga After Three Decades
pib.summary: The release reported the reintroduction of the endangered Red-Crowned Roofed Turtle into the Ganga ecosystem after no confirmed report of an adult in the river’s main channel for about 30 years. Twenty turtles were transferred from the Garhaita Turtle Conservation Center and released into the Haiderpur Wetland, with sonic devices attached for monitoring.

pib.headline: TARGETS ACHIEVED UNDER NAMAMI GANGE MISSION
pib.summary: The National Mission for Clean Ganga reported that 212 sewerage-infrastructure projects had been taken up to remediate polluted river areas, with a treatment capacity of 6,540 MLD. The release stated that 136 STP projects with a capacity of 3,780 MLD had been completed and made operational.

pib.headline: ALLOCATION OF FUNDS UNDER NMCG
pib.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti stated that the Namami Gange Programme was extended through March 2026 and outlined its budgetary allocations since inception. Total allocation from financial year 2014-15 through 2025-26 was reported at ₹26,824.86 crore, including ₹3,400 crore in Budget Estimates for 2025-26.

cag.finding: Of the 97 sewage treatment plant (STP) projects, only 46 were completed and functional by 2022. 23 STPs non-operational despite being shown as complete. Total sewage untreated remained 9,000 MLD per day.
cag.parameter: STPs operational vs planned
cag.actual: 46 STPs functional; 9,000 MLD untreated sewage

cag.finding: Industrial effluent discharge uncontrolled: Only 215 of 764 grossly polluting industries along Ganga were compliant with discharge norms. 72% of polluters continued dumping untreated waste.
cag.parameter: Industrial compliance with discharge norms
cag.actual: 28% industries compliant

cag.finding: The State Ganga Committee and State Mission for Clean Ganga did not plan and implement sewage treatment infrastructure in collaboration with local communities. Many Sewage Treatment Plants remained unconnected or only partially connected to household sewer networks, existing treatment capacity was insufficient, and significant quantities of untreated sewage were discharged into the Ganga. Eighteen STPs were not taken over by the maintenance agency because of operational and safety-related deficiencies.
cag.parameter: Sewage treatment infrastructure and operation of Sewage Treatment Plants

verdict.name: Namami Gange Programme
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 2 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: Saubhagya (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana)
scheme.description: Scheme to provide electricity connections to all un-electrified households in rural areas and poor households in urban areas. Replaced RGGVY.
scheme.goals: Achieve universal household electrification by December 2018. Provide free electricity connections to BPL families.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: All un-electrified households: approximately 4 crore households

pib.headline: Saubhagya: 2.37 crore households electrified in 15 months
pib.summary: Power Ministry announces that 2.37 crore households received electricity connections under Saubhagya in record time.

pib.headline: India achieves 100% household electrification: Saubhagya complete
pib.summary: Union Power Minister announces all 2.82 crore un-electrified households have been electrified under Saubhagya scheme, completing India's electrification mission.

pib.headline: SAUBHAGYA completes four years with 2.82 crore households electrified
pib.summary: The Ministry of Power reported that 2.82 crore households had been electrified under SAUBHAGYA through March 31, 2021. It also stated that previously unwilling households in seven states were later covered after expressing willingness to receive connections.

pib.headline: SAUBHAGYA implementation status shows 2.86 crore households electrified
pib.summary: The government reported that all seven states with subsequently identified willing households had achieved 100% household electrification by March 31, 2021. Overall, 2.86 crore households had been electrified through SAUBHAGYA and associated support under DDUGJY.

pib.headline: Guidelines issued for leftover households identified before SAUBHAGYA
pib.summary: The Ministry of Power said that approximately 19.09 lakh households identified before March 31, 2019 had initially declined connections but later expressed willingness to receive them. Guidelines were issued to cover any remaining households under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme, while states and union territories signed commitments related to 24x7 power supply.
pib.figureUnit: households that later expressed willingness for electrification

pib.headline: Rural electrification update reports 2.86 crore SAUBHAGYA connections
pib.summary: The Ministry of Power stated that 2.817 crore households had been electrified under SAUBHAGYA through March 2021, with additional households subsequently covered. The total reported number of households electrified reached 2.86 crore.

pib.headline: SAUBHAGYA electrified 2.86 crore households and closed in 2022
pib.summary: The government reported that 2.86 crore households were electrified under SAUBHAGYA, including households that became willing to receive connections after initially declining. The scheme was reported as closed on March 31, 2022, with further left-out electrification to be addressed through RDSS.

pib.headline: SAUBHAGYA scheme electrified 2.86 crore households
pib.summary: The Ministry of Power reiterated that 2.86 crore households had been electrified under SAUBHAGYA, including additional households that later expressed willingness for connections. It also reported that the scheme had closed on March 31, 2022, after sanctioned works were completed.

pib.headline: Household electrification under SAUBHAGYA reaches 2.86 crore
pib.summary: The Ministry of Power stated that all willing un-electrified rural households and all willing poor urban households had been provided electricity connections under SAUBHAGYA. The total number of households provided connections was reported as 2.86 crore, with RDSS support available for households left out.

pib.headline: Maharashtra SAUBHAGYA electrification details reported
pib.summary: The government reported that approximately 2.86 crore households had been electrified nationally under SAUBHAGYA through March 31, 2022, and that all sanctioned works were complete. In Maharashtra, 589,242 households were electrified through grid and off-grid modes.

pib.headline: SAUBHAGYA period completed with 2.86 crore households electrified
pib.summary: The Ministry of Power stated that all sanctioned SAUBHAGYA works had been completed and the scheme stood closed as of March 31, 2022. States reported that approximately 2.86 crore households received electricity connections, while remaining eligible households are being supported through RDSS and other programs.

pib.headline: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana
pib.summary: Under Saubhagya, 286 lakh households were electrified across the country against an estimated 300 lakh un-electrified households, and all States reported 100% electrification of willing households identified before March 31, 2019. The release also updates electrification works sanctioned under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme for additional households, including PVTG, tribal, Scheduled Caste, and remote-area households.

cag.finding: Performance audit of DDUGJY and Saubhagya in Mizoram found deficiencies in implementation of the schemes by the Power and Electricity Department.
cag.parameter: Implementation of rural infrastructure and household electrification schemes
cag.actual: CAG identified deficiencies in planning, execution, financial management and monitoring.
cag.reportExcerpt: Even though the State Government has stated 100 per cent (in excess of 100 per cent in case of Saubhagya Scheme) achievement of the broad objectives in terms of electrification of targeted number of villages, habitations and households, creation of electric infrastructure, etc., Audit observed that the schemes could have been more efficiently and economically implemented had due diligence been exercised in matters related to planning, execution and monitoring.

cag.finding: Assam Power Distribution Company Limited did not undertake feeder-segregation works, and implementation suffered from delays, weak monitoring, irregular contracting and procurement of substandard items.
cag.parameter: Feeder segregation and compliance with scheme implementation requirements
cag.actual: Feeder segregation was not undertaken, preventing achievement of the objective of optimum power rostering between agricultural and non-agricultural consumers.
cag.reportExcerpt: The Company did not take up feeder segregation works resulting in non-achievement of the objective of optimum rostering of power between agricultural and non-agricultural consumers. Implementation of the scheme was also characterized by several instances of non-adherence to the scheme guidelines. There were instances of inefficiencies in contract management, execution of works and monitoring. Project implementation was beset with slow execution of works, weak monitoring, non-fulfilment of commitments made in the agreements, delays in award of contracts, irregular award of work, procurement of items of below standard etc.

cag.finding: Karnataka's implementation audit found incomplete and deficient Saubhagya works, including execution without sanctioned estimates, discrepancies in material inspection and excess payment to contractors.
cag.parameter: Completion, authorization, quality control and payment accuracy for Saubhagya works
cag.actual: CAG found unauthorized execution, material-inspection discrepancies and excess payments during implementation.
cag.reportExcerpt: 3.10 Execution of works under SAUBHAGYA

cag.finding: Madhya Pradesh's audit of Saubhagya found deficient project execution, excess expenditure and procurement, infrastructure created without connections, non-compliant solar power-pack installations and incorrect claims for cash awards and additional grants.
cag.parameter: Compliance, cost efficiency and achievement of household electrification outputs under Saubhagya
cag.actual: CAG found irregular awards, deficient execution, excess procurement and expenditure, infrastructure without service connections, and incorrect grant-related claims.
cag.reportExcerpt: Deficient execution of Contract

cag.finding: Performance audit of DDUGJY and Saubhagya in Tripura identified deficiencies in planning, implementation, household electrification, feeder separation, financial management and monitoring.
cag.parameter: Implementation of rural electrification schemes and achievement of household electrification objectives
cag.actual: CAG reported significant implementation deficiencies across the audited scheme components.
cag.reportExcerpt: The Performance Audit of DDUGJY and Saubhagya in Tripura revealed deficiencies in planning, implementation, household electrification, feeder separation, financial management and monitoring.

cag.finding: In Jharkhand, 284,485 Saubhagya connections were released in seven test-checked districts against work orders for 406,196 connections, without ensuring assessment of beneficiaries eligible for free connections.
cag.parameter: Saubhagya household connections released versus connections covered by work orders
cag.reportExcerpt: Under SAUBHAGYA, 2,84,485 connections were released in the seven test-checked districts against work order for providing 4,06,196 connections without ensuring assessment of beneficiaries eligible for free connections.

cag.finding: Arunachal Pradesh's performance audit of DDUGJY and Saubhagya revealed several deficiencies in planning, execution, financial management and monitoring of rural electrification works.
cag.parameter: Achievement of rural electrification and household-connection objectives
cag.actual: CAG reported deficiencies in implementation of both schemes.
cag.reportExcerpt: A Performance Audit of the Implementation of Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Joyti Yojana and Saubhagya scheme in Arunachal Pradesh carried out covering the period from 2014-15 to 2020-21, revealed several deficiencies in implementation of programme/schemes which are highlighted below:

cag.finding: The Union-level performance audit found systemic deficiencies in DDUGJY and Saubhagya implementation, including incomplete electrification, weak planning and monitoring, financial irregularities, inadequate quality assurance and failure to fully achieve scheme objectives.
cag.parameter: Achievement of rural infrastructure, household electrification, financial management and quality-assurance objectives
cag.actual: CAG identified deficiencies across implementation, financial management, quality assurance and monitoring of Saubhagya projects in test-checked States and Union Territories.
cag.reportExcerpt: The objective of strengthening and augmentation of sub-transmission & distribution infrastructure and feeder separation for reliable and quality power supply after electrification of un-electrified villages in rural areas was, therefore, partially achieved as the allocated budget outlay was insufficient to meet the objectives of DDUGJY scheme with respect to system strengthening and feeder separation.

cag.finding: Uttar Pradesh issued an indent for electrification of 1.70 crore un-electrified households, but REC approved only 1.22 crore connections; the audit also found that off-grid connections were omitted from DPRs and identified irregularities in execution and beneficiary selection.
cag.parameter: Households proposed for electrification versus connections approved under Saubhagya
cag.reportExcerpt: Despite the clear mandate to include off-grid connections under the SAUBHAGYA scheme, the DPRs omitted such provisions.

verdict.name: Saubhagya (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana)
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 4 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: Ayushman Bharat – PM Jan Arogya Yojana
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
scheme.description: World's largest health insurance scheme providing health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. Renamed from RSBY.
scheme.goals: Cover 10 crore poor and vulnerable families (approximately 50 crore beneficiaries) for health expenses. Reduce out-of-pocket health expenditure.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 10 crore families from bottom 40% of Indian population

pib.headline: PM launches Ayushman Bharat: Rs 5 lakh coverage for 50 crore
pib.summary: PM Modi launches Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana providing Rs 5 lakh annual health cover to 10 crore families or 50 crore beneficiaries.

pib.headline: 18 crore Ayushman cards issued to beneficiaries
pib.summary: Ministry of Health announces issuance of 18 crore Ayushman Bharat cards, with 2.3 crore hospitalisations covered.

pib.headline: Ayushman Bharat: 3 crore hospitalisations covered
pib.summary: On the 4th anniversary, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY has covered over 3 crore hospitalisations, providing free healthcare worth Rs 35,000 crore.

pib.headline: 5 crore hospital admissions authorized under AB-PMJAY
pib.summary: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY reached 5 crore authorized hospital admissions, representing treatment worth Rs. 61,501 crore. The release also reported that 23.39 crore beneficiaries had been verified and could access cashless treatment through 28,351 empanelled hospitals.

pib.headline: 30 crore Ayushman cards created
pib.summary: AB-PMJAY crossed the milestone of 30 crore Ayushman cards created as of January 12, 2024. The release attributed the acceleration to campaigns including Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra and Ayushman Bhava, as well as the Ayushman mobile app.

pib.headline: More than 34.7 crore Ayushman cards created
pib.summary: The government reported that more than 34.7 crore Ayushman cards had been created under AB-PMJAY as of June 30, 2024. It also stated that 7.37 crore hospital admissions worth approximately Rs. 1 lakh crore had been authorized.

pib.headline: AB-PMJAY expanded to senior citizens aged 70 and above
pib.summary: The government reiterated the expansion of AB-PMJAY to provide free treatment benefits of up to Rs. 5 lakh annually to all citizens aged 70 and above, regardless of socioeconomic status. As of November 30, 2024, approximately 36 crore beneficiaries had been verified and 8.39 crore hospital admissions had been authorized.
pib.figureUnit: senior citizens aged 70 years and above covered by the expansion

pib.headline: Ayushman Vay Vandana benefits available through expanded hospital network
pib.summary: The release provided an update on treatment services available to senior citizens under the Ayushman Vay Vandana Card following the AB-PMJAY expansion. It stated that beneficiaries could access cashless services covering 1,961 procedures across 27 specialties through more than 30,072 hospitals.

pib.headline: AB-PMJAY savings exceed Rs. 1.25 lakh crore
pib.summary: The Economic Survey 2024-25 reported that government-supported health insurance schemes including AB-PMJAY had helped reduce out-of-pocket expenditure. It recorded savings of more than Rs. 1.25 lakh crore and noted that government health expenditure increased while the share paid directly by households declined.
pib.figureUnit: rupees in reported savings on out-of-pocket expenditure

pib.headline: Over 41 crore Ayushman cards created
pib.summary: The government reported that more than 41 crore Ayushman cards had been created under AB-PMJAY. The scheme had 31,466 empanelled hospitals and more than 9.84 crore authorized hospital admissions worth over Rs. 1.40 lakh crore.

pib.headline: More than 15,733 private hospitals empanelled under AB-PMJAY
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that more than 15,733 private hospitals had been empanelled under AB-PMJAY as of December 31, 2025. It also stated that 1,259 of these private hospitals were located in aspirational districts.

pib.headline: 43.52 crore Ayushman cards created
pib.summary: The government reported that 43.52 crore Ayushman cards had been created under AB-PMJAY as of February 28, 2026, including 1.14 crore Ayushman Vay Vandana cards. It also reported 11.69 crore authorized hospital admissions worth Rs. 1.73 lakh crore and 36,229 empanelled hospitals.

pib.headline: West Bengal Set to Become the 36th State/UT to Implement Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
pib.summary: The National Health Authority and the Government of West Bengal were scheduled to sign a Memorandum of Understanding for implementing AB PM-JAY in the state. The implementation would make West Bengal the 36th State/Union Territory covered by the scheme and extend health coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year to eligible beneficiaries.

pib.headline: West Bengal Becomes 36th State/UT to Implement Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
pib.summary: West Bengal became the 36th State/Union Territory to implement Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY after the National Health Authority signed an MoU with the state government. The inclusion is expected to extend health-assurance benefits to approximately 1.43 crore families and improve access to cashless treatment nationwide.

cag.finding: The audit found substantial shortfalls in beneficiary verification and coverage under AB-PMJAY in Bihar. Against the revised target of 61.8 million beneficiaries, only 25.6 million had been verified by 31 March 2024. In addition, 595 villages with eligible beneficiaries had no Ayushman Cards issued.
cag.parameter: AB-PMJAY beneficiary verification and coverage
cag.claimed: Coverage target of 12.1 million beneficiary families, representing approximately 61.8 million beneficiaries
cag.actual: Only 25.6 million beneficiaries verified by 31 March 2024; 595 eligible villages had no Ayushman Card holders
cag.reportExcerpt: The PMJAY scheme aimed to provide health cover to all the targeted 1.21 crore beneficiary families of the State. Audit noted that against the revised target of 6.18 crore beneficiaries, only 2.56 crore beneficiaries (41 per cent) were verified by the State as on 31 March 2024. Further, 595 villages having eligible beneficiaries had no Ayushman Cards issued.

cag.finding: CAG found significant data quality issues in the beneficiary database. In 7 sample states, 7.49 lakh beneficiary families were found ineligible or duplicate, yet they received benefits worth Rs 491 crore.
cag.parameter: Beneficiary database integrity
cag.actual: 7.49 lakh ineligible families benefited

cag.finding: Only 2.95 crore of the targeted 10 crore families had been issued Ayushman cards as of 2022. Coverage of intended beneficiaries was only 29.5%.
cag.parameter: Beneficiary card issuance
cag.actual: 2.95 crore families with active cards

cag.finding: Hospitals empanelled under PMJAY performed fraudulent claims. CAG identified 7,491 suspicious transactions worth Rs 88.36 crore — payments made after patient death, treatments impossible in the empanelled facility type.
cag.parameter: Claims fraud prevention
cag.actual: Rs 88.36 crore in fraudulent claims detected

cag.finding: Under Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY), inordinate delay in payment of insurance claims to beneficiaries was noticed. A District Implementation Unit to support PMJAY and a combined state-level unit for anti-fraud, medical audit and vigilance with district-level officers were not formed.
cag.parameter: Claims processing and programme governance
cag.actual: Inordinate delay in payment of insurance claims; required district and state-level implementation, anti-fraud, medical audit and vigilance units were not formed.

verdict.name: Ayushman Bharat – PM Jan Arogya Yojana
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 2 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
scheme.description: India's flagship demand-driven skill certification scheme, now in its fourth phase (2022–26). Trains youth in industry-relevant short-term courses (STT) and certifies existing workers through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL). Run through a network of NSDC-accredited training centres and Skill India Digital Hub.
scheme.goals: PMKVY 1.0 (2015-16): 24 lakh candidates. PMKVY 2.0 (2016-20): 1 crore candidates, ₹12,000 crore. PMKVY 3.0 (2020-21): 8 lakh candidates, ₹948 crore. PMKVY 4.0 (2022-26): Industry 4.0 skills (AI, drones, green energy, coding) with on-the-job training, ₹6,000 crore; cumulative target of 1.4 crore additional candidates.
