pib.headline: PMKVY: 1.07 crore youth skilled in 3 years, 68% placement rate
pib.summary: MSDE announces 1.07 crore candidates trained under PMKVY since 2015. Ministry claims 68% placement rate for trained candidates.

pib.headline: PMKVY 3.0: 8 lakh candidates to be trained, Rs 948 crore allocated
pib.summary: MSDE launches PMKVY 3.0 with target to train 8 lakh candidates over 2020-21. Focus on new age skills like AI, robotics, IoT.

pib.headline: UNDER PRADHAN MANTRI KAUSHAL VIKAS YOJANA SCHEME, since 2015 till 30.6.2024, 1.48 crore candidates have been trained/oriented
pib.summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship reported that 1.48 crore candidates had been trained or oriented under PMKVY from its launch in 2015 through June 30, 2024. It also stated that 24.3 lakh of 56.88 lakh candidates certified under the first three versions were reported placed, a 42.8% placement rate.

pib.headline: Under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, skill development training has been imparted through Short-Term Training and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning
pib.summary: The release said that 24.38 lakh candidates had been reported placed under PMKVY 1.0 to 3.0 as of June 30, 2024, including both self-employed and wage-employed candidates. It noted that placement tracking was delinked from PMKVY 4.0.

pib.headline: Building a Future-Ready India
pib.summary: The release described PMKVY as a flagship Skill India Mission programme providing free short-duration training and incentives for skill certification. It reported that the scheme had trained or oriented 1.48 crore candidates since 2015 through June 30, 2024, while PMKVY 4.0 was being implemented for financial years 2022–2026.

pib.headline: 1,60,33,081 candidates have been trained/oriented under the PMKVY scheme from 2015 to 2024
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that 1,60,33,081 candidates had been trained or oriented under PMKVY from 2015 through December 31, 2024. The release also stated that the reported placement rate among Short-Term Training-certified candidates through PMKVY 3.0 was 43%, while PMKVY 4.0 emphasizes career pathways rather than placement tracking.

pib.headline: Flagship Skills Mission
pib.summary: The release stated that 24,37,887 candidates were reported placed nationwide under the Short-Term Training component of PMKVY 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0. It added that PMKVY 4.0 focuses on helping trained candidates choose varied career paths and includes digital tools such as the Skill India Digital Hub.

pib.headline: Skill Development in Future Technologies and Job Placement
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that PMKVY had aligned more than 200 new-age and future-skills job roles with Industry 4.0 requirements, including AI/ML, robotics, electric vehicles, mechatronics and drone technology. Up to June 30, 2025, 4,32,712 candidates had been trained in these PMKVY job roles.

pib.headline: Climate-Resilient Employment Planning
pib.summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship states that PMKVY includes agriculture and allied-sector job roles addressing climate-related challenges such as heat stress, crop failure and desertification. These programs are intended to support labour transition and climate-resilient livelihoods in vulnerable regions.

pib.headline: PMKVY Training and Employment Outcomes
pib.summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship reports that PMKVY 4.0 uses market-oriented and demand-driven training, with on-the-job training embedded in industry-relevant courses. The release also explains that placement tracking applied to the first three PMKVY versions, while PMKVY 4.0 focuses on helping trained candidates pursue varied career paths.

pib.headline: Year End Review 2025: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
pib.summary: The Ministry’s year-end review states that PMKVY 4.0 had trained candidates across 38 sectors and 36 States by December 2025. It also highlights expanded future-skill courses, Skill Hubs, institutional participation and convergence with other national missions.

pib.headline: Skill India Digital Hub
pib.summary: The release describes the Skill India Digital Hub as a platform integrating training, assessment, certification and related skilling services. It reports that PMKVY 4.0 trained and certified candidates in the Chatra Parliamentary Constituency of Jharkhand, alongside broader onboarding of candidates and stakeholders onto the platform.

pib.headline: Generating Job-Ready Youth under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana
pib.summary: The Ministry reports that PMKVY has trained or oriented candidates nationwide since 2015, with certified candidates forming a substantial portion of the total. For PMKVY 1.0 to 3.0, the release reports placements among Short-Term Training candidates, while PMKVY 4.0 emphasizes career choice, self-employment and wage employment through industry-relevant courses and on-the-job training.

pib.headline: Skill Development in AI, Digital and Emerging Technologies
pib.summary: The Ministry states that PMKVY 4.0 offers courses in artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, drones, industrial IoT and other emerging fields. According to Skill India Digital Hub data, candidates had been trained in futuristic job roles, with funding allocated for digital-skills training.

pib.headline: Jobs for Skill Trained Youth
pib.summary: The Ministry reports cumulative PMKVY training figures through December 2025 and explains that placement tracking was conducted for the Short-Term Training component of PMKVY 1.0 to 3.0. It also cites an evaluation showing an increase in the combined share of employed and self-employed respondents after PMKVY 4.0 training.
pib.figureUnit: employed or self-employed STT respondents after training

pib.headline: Strengthening Skill Development Ecosystem
pib.summary: The Ministry outlines measures under PMKVY 4.0 to expand quality, transparency and industry relevance through the Skill India Digital Hub and industry-led training. It highlights future-skill training in areas including artificial intelligence, robotics, cloud computing, IoT and green technologies, while noting reported placements under PMKVY 1.0 to 3.0.

pib.headline: Skilling for Space and Geospatial Sectors
pib.summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is promoting skill development in space and geospatial technologies through PMKVY, NAPS and related initiatives. IN-SPACe has introduced 11 short-term space-technology courses, through which more than 1,000 candidates have been trained nationwide.

cag.finding: Bank account details on the Skill India Portal were missing, blank, null, or invalid for 90.66 lakh out of 95.90 lakh certified beneficiaries under PMKVY 2.0 and 3.0 — 94.53% of all records. Invalid entries included placeholder values such as '11111111111', '123456', single-digit numbers, and text/names/special characters. 12,122 account numbers were reused across 52,381 different candidates; one account number was shared by 2,106 individuals.
cag.parameter: Beneficiary data integrity — bank account records on Skill India Portal
cag.actual: 90.66 lakh (94.53%) had missing or invalid bank data
cag.reportExcerpt: Bank account details, which are mandatory for Direct Benefit Transfers, were missing, blank, marked Null/N/A, or filled with zeros in 94.53 per cent of 95.90 lakh beneficiary records under PMKVY 2.0 and 3.0. Among available records, 12,122 account numbers were repeated for at least 52,381 candidates; entries such as '11111111111', '123456', single-digit numbers, or fields populated with text, names or special characters were recorded.

cag.finding: Certified training was claimed by multiple defunct companies on the Skill India Portal. Radiate Designs (struck off by Registrar of Companies in 2015) certified 15,218 people. Neelima Moving Pictures (shut for 5–6 years) claimed to have trained 33,000 people. Present Media Private Limited certified 19,561 candidates as dancers, hairdressers, and makeup artists across nine states. At least one training partner (Jaipur Cultural Society) claimed to have conducted training on 31st February — a date that does not exist. Identical photographs were submitted as training evidence in multiple states simultaneously (Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan).
cag.parameter: Ghost training centres and fraudulent certification
cag.reportExcerpt: Field inspections revealed instances where training centres were found closed on dates SIP data indicated training was scheduled. Identical photographs were submitted as evidence for multiple beneficiaries across different states. Certifications were issued by entities struck off by the Registrar of Companies prior to the audit period.

cag.finding: Thousands of underage candidates were enrolled and certified in violation of PMKVY eligibility criteria. Over 52,000 candidates were certified as Group Farming Practitioners without meeting the minimum age requirement. Over 40,000 underage candidates were certified as Self-Employed Tailors. Similar violations were found across multiple other job roles. DBT incentive payments of ₹500 had not been received by 34 lakh certified candidates as of October 2024, despite the relevant phases having formally concluded. DBT was successful for only 18.44% of certified candidates as of 2023.
cag.parameter: Underage enrolments and DBT payment failures
cag.claimed: 95.90 lakh certified candidates to receive ₹500 DBT incentive
cag.actual: Only 18.44% received DBT in 2023; 34 lakh unpaid as of Oct 2024
cag.reportExcerpt: Despite minimum age and qualification requirements for various job roles, thousands of underage candidates were enrolled and certified. More than 52,000 candidates were certified as Group Farming Practitioners and over 40,000 as Self-Employed Tailors without meeting age criteria. DBT payments were processed for only 25.58 per cent of certified candidates, with successful payouts in just 18.44 per cent of cases as of 2023.

cag.finding: Out of 56 lakh candidates certified under the Short-Term Training and Special Projects components of PMKVY, only 23 lakh candidates were placed, representing 41 per cent placement.
cag.parameter: Placement of candidates certified under PMKVY
cag.actual: 23 lakh placed candidates

cag.finding: Failure of the Kerala Academy for Skills Excellence to ensure the genuineness of placement documents submitted by training partners resulted in undue financial benefit of ₹16.72 lakh to the training partners under PMKVY.
cag.parameter: Verification of placement claims and placement-linked payments
cag.actual: 16.72 lakh undue financial benefit

cag.finding: MSDE sanctioned ₹1,088.73 lakh under PMKVY for training and placement of 7,071 youths during 2017-18; the Department had incurred expenditure of ₹776.81 lakh as of 4 August 2019.
cag.parameter: Utilisation of funds sanctioned for PMKVY training and placement

cag.finding: The audit found that adherence to PMKVY guidelines relating to biometric attendance, insurance of candidates, organising Kaushal Melas, and training linked to captive placements was not maintained or complied with; monitoring, inspection and internal control mechanisms were also ineffective.
cag.parameter: PMKVY guideline compliance, monitoring and internal controls

cag.finding: The report included a Subject Specific Compliance Audit on Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 2.0 under the Skill Development and Employment Department, Government of Uttarakhand.
cag.parameter: PMKVY 2.0 compliance

cag.finding: The report showed a budget allocation of ₹2,676.65 crore for Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana against expenditure of ₹2,112.67 crore, resulting in savings of ₹563.98 crore, or 21.07 per cent of the allocation.
cag.parameter: Budget allocation and expenditure under PMKVY

verdict.name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 3 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: PM Ujjwala Yojana
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
scheme.renamedFrom: Rajiv Gandhi Gramin LPG Vitaran Yojana
scheme.description: Scheme to provide free LPG connections to women from BPL households. Aims to replace unclean cooking fuels with clean LPG.
scheme.goals: Provide 8 crore LPG connections to BPL women by 2020. Safeguard health of women and children from pollution caused by traditional cooking fuels.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Women from BPL households across rural India

pib.headline: PM Ujjwala: 8 crore LPG connections target achieved ahead of schedule
pib.summary: PM Modi announces achievement of 8 crore free LPG connections target 7 months ahead of schedule. Clean cooking fuel reaches every village.

pib.headline: Ujjwala beneficiaries: 14.17 crore LPG connections in rural India
pib.summary: During COVID, free LPG cylinders given to Ujjwala beneficiaries. Over 14.17 crore total LPG connections in rural areas.

pib.headline: Features of PMUY
pib.summary: The release describes PMUY's provision of deposit-free LPG connections to adult women from poor households. It reports that the original target of 8 crore connections was achieved in September 2019 and that Ujjwala 2.0 had expanded access to remaining households.

pib.headline: Cabinet approves 75 lakh additional Ujjwala connections
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved extending PMUY to provide 75 lakh additional LPG connections during FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26. The release said this would increase the total number of PMUY beneficiaries to 10.35 crore.

pib.headline: Delivery of LPG cylinders to urban slum dwellers
pib.summary: The release explains that PMUY provides deposit-free LPG connections to eligible poor households, including qualifying urban slum residents. It reports that 9.59 crore PMUY connections had been released as of September 30, 2023.

pib.headline: Continuation of targeted subsidy for PMUY consumers in FY 2024-25
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of a targeted subsidy of Rs.300 per 14.2 kg cylinder for up to 12 refills per year during FY 2024-25. The release stated that more than 10.27 crore PMUY beneficiaries were eligible and that the total expenditure would be Rs.12,000 crore.

pib.headline: Aadhaar authentication improves targeting under PAHAL and Ujjwala
pib.summary: The release says Aadhaar-based authentication is being used to identify, authenticate and remove duplicate beneficiaries under PMUY and PAHAL. It describes the measure as a way to improve the accuracy and efficiency of subsidy delivery.

pib.headline: 75 lakh additional PMUY connections completed
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that Oil Marketing Companies had completed releasing the additional 75 lakh PMUY connections approved in September 2023. As of July 1, 2024, the country had 10.33 crore LPG connections under PMUY.

pib.headline: Distribution of LPG connections to eligible beneficiaries
pib.summary: The release outlines eligibility categories and verification mechanisms for receiving PMUY connections, including Aadhaar authentication and duplicate-checking systems. It reported 10.33 crore PMUY beneficiaries as of November 1, 2024.

pib.headline: Year-end review: PMUY reaches 10.33 crore connections
pib.summary: The Ministry's year-end review reported that PMUY had released 10.33 crore LPG connections. It also stated that approximately 222 crore LPG refills had been delivered to PMUY households since the scheme began.

pib.headline: Government steps to ensure affordable LPG
pib.summary: The release summarizes the expansion of Ujjwala 2.0 and the subsequent 75 lakh connection program, noting that both targets had been achieved. It reported 10.33 crore PMUY beneficiaries as of March 1, 2025.

pib.headline: Government steps to encourage better LPG consumption by PMUY beneficiaries
pib.summary: The release describes measures intended to make LPG more affordable and encourage sustained use among PMUY beneficiaries, including subsidies, smaller-cylinder options and awareness campaigns. It reported that average per-capita consumption increased to 4.47 refills in FY 2024-25.
pib.figureUnit: average LPG refills per PMUY beneficiary household in FY 2024-25

pib.headline: Continuation of targeted PMUY subsidy for FY 2025-26
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a targeted subsidy of Rs.300 per 14.2 kg cylinder for up to nine refills per year for PMUY beneficiaries during FY 2025-26. The approved expenditure was Rs.12,000 crore, with about 10.33 crore PMUY connections reported as of July 1, 2025.

pib.headline: Government approves 25 lakh additional Ujjwala connections
pib.summary: The Government approved the release of 25 lakh additional deposit-free LPG connections under PMUY during FY 2025-26. The measure was intended to clear pending applications and advance universal access to clean cooking fuel.

pib.headline: PAHAL (DBTL) Scheme Delivers Improved Efficiency, Transparency, and Consumer-Centric Reforms
pib.summary: The release states that biometric Aadhaar authentication had been completed for 69% of existing PMUY beneficiaries as of November 1, 2025. It also reports that 8.63 lakh PMUY connections had been terminated through deduplication and related verification measures.

pib.headline: Government Approves 25 Lakh Additional LPG Connections Under PMUY for FY 2025-26
pib.summary: The Government approved 25 lakh additional LPG connections under PMUY during FY 2025-26 to clear pending applications and achieve saturation of LPG access. The release also says eligibility was simplified to allow adult women from poor households to apply through a Deprivation Declaration.

pib.headline: Year End Review 2025: Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas — Ujjwala Yojana Continues to Expand Clean Cooking Access across the Country
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that PMUY beneficiaries reached about 10.35 crore as of December 1, 2025. It also highlighted the approval of 25 lakh additional connections, simplified eligibility procedures, and a targeted subsidy of ₹300 per 14.2 kg cylinder for up to nine refills annually.

cag.finding: CAG found that only 3.66 crore out of 8 crore Ujjwala beneficiaries refilled their cylinders even once. 54% of LPG connections were effectively dormant by end of 2018.
cag.parameter: Cylinder refill rate (actual LPG usage)
cag.actual: 45.75% connections refilled at least once

cag.finding: Average LPG consumption by Ujjwala beneficiaries was 3.21 refills per year against national average of 7.7. Beneficiaries still using firewood due to cost of cylinder refill.
cag.parameter: Annual LPG consumption per beneficiary
cag.claimed: Similar to national average of 7.7 refills/year
cag.actual: 3.21 refills per year
cag.reportExcerpt: Encouraging the sustained usage of LPG remains a big challenge as the annual average refill consumption of PMUY consumers on 31 December 2018 was only 3.21. Since the cost of refill has to be paid upfront by the BPL consumers, this has become a constraint in ensuring sustained usage of LPG.

verdict.name: PM Ujjwala Yojana
verdict.summary: Accountability concerns: 1 critical and 1 major finding indicate the scheme is not meeting its stated objectives.

scheme.name: Digital India Programme
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
scheme.description: Flagship programme to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. Covers digital infrastructure, digital services, and digital literacy.

pib.headline: 5 lakh Common Service Centres operational across India
pib.summary: Over 5 lakh CSCs operational providing digital services to rural citizens. Over 3.5 lakh CSCs run by women.

pib.headline: BharatNet: 1.75 lakh gram panchayats connected with broadband
pib.summary: PM announces 1.75 lakh gram panchayats connected with high-speed broadband internet under BharatNet, flagship component of Digital India.

pib.headline: Digital India: 4 lakh crore digital transactions in 2021-22
pib.summary: IT Ministry announces India recorded 4 lakh crore digital transactions in FY22, making India the global leader in real-time digital payments.

pib.headline: Union Cabinet approves expansion of the Digital India programme with an outlay of ₹14,903 crore
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved expansion of the Digital India programme with a total outlay of ₹14,903 crore. The expansion includes reskilling 6.25 lakh IT professionals, training 2.65 lakh people in information security, adding 540 UMANG services, deploying nine supercomputers, and supporting 1,200 startups in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

pib.headline: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology launches Phase III of capacity-building initiatives under Digital India vision
pib.summary: MeitY launched the third phase of its capacity-building initiatives under the Digital India vision. The programmes cover Digital Public Infrastructure, artificial intelligence and machine learning, digital governance, data management, and management of large digital transformation projects; the regional programme began with 32 participants.

pib.headline: Future Ready: India’s Digital Economy to Contribute One-Fifth of National Income by 2029-30
pib.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology reported that India’s digital economy accounted for 11.74% of GDP in 2022-23 and employed 14.67 million workers. It is projected to grow to nearly one-fifth of national income by 2029-30, driven by digital platforms, artificial intelligence, cloud services, and wider digitalisation.

pib.headline: Government of India Expands AI-Driven Skilling; India AI Mission Gains Momentum with 67 Proposals for Indigenous AI Models; Digital India Bhashini Initiative Boosts AI-Powered Vernacular Language Accessibility
pib.summary: The release highlights the Government’s AI-for-All approach and progress under the IndiaAI Mission. It reports that 67 proposals were received for indigenous foundation models, while the Digital India Bhashini initiative is advancing access to AI-powered services in Indian languages.

pib.headline: NIELIT Signs MoUs with 8 Visionary Organizations to Propel Digital India Initiatives
pib.summary: NIELIT signed memorandums of understanding with eight organizations to strengthen education, skilling, research, and innovation in electronics and information technology. The collaborations cover joint research, curriculum development, capacity building, training, and emerging technologies.

pib.headline: Government’s Initiatives to Make Information Technology Accessible to Citizens Residing in Rural, Hilly and Remote Areas of the Country; Digital India Programme Bridging the Urban-Rural Divide
pib.summary: The release describes Digital India initiatives aimed at expanding digital infrastructure, delivering government services online, and improving digital literacy in rural, hilly, and remote areas. As of October 2025, 5.67 lakh Common Services Centres were functional nationwide, including 4.41 lakh at the Gram Panchayat level.

pib.headline: Digital India program has enabled wider access to digital services and opportunities; 400% increase in broadband subscribers over a decade
pib.summary: The release states that the Digital India programme has expanded access to digital services and opportunities across India. Broadband subscribers increased from 25 crore in 2014-15 to 103 crore in 2024-25, representing a 400% rise.

pib.headline: DigiLocker Experiences Massive Expansion: Electricity distribution utilities are now live for millions of consumers nationwide
pib.summary: DigiLocker has onboarded 68 electricity distribution companies and power departments across 35 States and Union Territories. The integration enables consumers to access issuer-sourced digital electricity bills through the DigiLocker application.
pib.figureUnit: electricity distribution companies and power departments

pib.headline: Mahasarathi (Family ID) Now on DigiLocker: 14 Crore Citizens Get Instant Digital Access
pib.summary: The release announces that residents of Maharashtra can access their Mahasarathi Family ID through DigiLocker. The initiative provides digital access to the identity document for approximately 14 crore residents.

pib.headline: Digital India Nears 11 Years, Driving India's Next Phase of Technology-Led Growth through Artificial Intelligence, Semiconductor Manufacturing, Digital Public Infrastructure and Affordable Digital Connectivity
pib.summary: The release reviews Digital India's progress and highlights investments in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure and connectivity. It reports that ₹1.64 lakh crore has been approved across 12 semiconductor projects and that a shared compute facility with more than 45,000 GPUs is strengthening India's AI ecosystem.
pib.figureUnit: lakh crore approved across semiconductor projects

pib.headline: 11 Years of Digital India: eSaras Online Market & Melas Strengthening Rural Livelihoods through Digital Commerce
pib.summary: The release describes eSaras, developed by the Digital India Corporation under MeitY in collaboration with the Ministry of Rural Development, as a digital marketplace for rural women-led enterprises and producer organisations. It reports that the platform supports more than 8.99 crore registered Self-Help Group members and offers over 1,400 products.

cag.claimed: Establishment of 2.5 lakh Common Service Centres at Gram Panchayat level

scheme.name: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik)

pib.headline: UDAN: 419 routes operationalised, 67 airports connected
pib.summary: Civil Aviation Ministry announces 419 UDAN routes operational connecting 67 airports. Over 1 crore passengers have flown on UDAN routes at subsidised fares.

pib.headline: Under UDAN, 453 routes have commenced, operationalizing 70 airports including 2 water aerodromes and 9 heliports
pib.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation reported that 453 UDAN routes had commenced, connecting 70 airports, water aerodromes and heliports as of November 29, 2022. More than 2.15 lakh UDAN flights had operated and over 1.1 crore passengers had benefited from the scheme.

pib.headline: 73 airports have been operationalized under the UDAN scheme till January 2023
pib.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation stated that 73 unserved or underserved airports, including heliports and water aerodromes, had been operationalized under UDAN as of January 31, 2023. Approximately Rs. 2,355 crore in Viability Gap Funding had been released to selected airline operators.

pib.headline: 469 routes connecting 74 airports operationalised under UDAN Scheme
pib.summary: As of February 28, 2023, 469 UDAN routes connecting 74 unserved and underserved airports had been operationalized. The release also reported that around Rs. 2,433 crore in Viability Gap Funding had been released to selected airline operators.

pib.headline: 479 RCS-UDAN routes operational connecting 74 airports, including 2 water aerodromes and 9 heliports
pib.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation reported that 479 UDAN routes were operational as of June 30, 2023, connecting 74 airports, water aerodromes and heliports. More than 123 lakh passengers had benefited, while Rs. 2,729.11 crore in Viability Gap Funding had been released.

pib.headline: UDAN Version 5: 5.0, 5.1 and 5.2
pib.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation highlighted six years of UDAN and reported that more than 130 lakh passengers had benefited from the scheme. It also described successive versions of UDAN, including changes expanding helicopter connectivity, tourism routes and operational flexibility.

pib.headline: 519 routes operationalised under RCS-UDAN Scheme, including 53 tourism and 48 helicopter routes
pib.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation reported that 519 UDAN routes had been operationalized, including tourism and helicopter routes. More than 133.86 lakh passengers had benefited, 2.56 lakh flights had operated, and 13 airlines had commenced UDAN operations.

pib.headline: The Journey of UDAN: Soaring Towards Inclusivity in Indian Aviation
pib.summary: The release reviewed UDAN's development since its launch in 2016 and its role in improving affordable regional air connectivity. It described the scheme's market-driven model, Viability Gap Funding and concessions provided by airport operators and governments to support service to underserved regions.

pib.headline: Year End Review 2024: UDAN turns 8, connecting India with 619 routes and 88 operational airports
pib.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation's year-end review reported that UDAN had connected 88 operational airports through 619 routes by the end of 2024. The review presented this expansion as part of broader improvements in India's regional air connectivity and aviation infrastructure.

pib.headline: UDAN Scheme: Connecting India, One Flight at a Time
pib.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation reported that 625 UDAN routes had been operationalized, connecting 90 airports, including water aerodromes and heliports. More than 1.49 crore passengers had benefited, and Rs. 4,023.37 crore had been disbursed as Viability Gap Funding.

pib.headline: Cabinet approves Modified UDAN to deepen regional connectivity and expand inclusive air access across India
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the launch and implementation of Modified UDAN for a ten-year period from FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36. The scheme has a total outlay of Rs. 28,840 crore and proposes development of 100 airports, support for approximately 441 aerodromes and 200 modern helipads.

cag.finding: Up to UDAN-3, 52 per cent (403 out of 774 routes) of the awarded routes could not commence operations.
cag.parameter: Commencement of operations on awarded UDAN routes
cag.actual: 403 of 774 awarded routes could not commence operations

verdict.name: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik)
verdict.summary: 1 major CAG finding indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan
scheme.description: Integrated scheme for school education extending from pre-school to Class 12. Treats school education holistically without segmentation.
scheme.goals: Universal access to quality education. Improve learning outcomes. Reduce gender and social category gaps. Transition rate from primary to upper primary to 90%.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: All school-going children from pre-primary to Class 12

pib.headline: Samagra Shiksha: Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher secondary reaches 57.6%
pib.summary: Education Ministry announces GER in higher secondary education has risen to 57.6% under Samagra Shiksha, up from 56.5%.

pib.headline: Universalisation of quality Education under SSA
pib.summary: The Ministry of Education describes Samagra Shiksha as an integrated scheme covering school education from pre-school through Class 12. It outlines the scheme’s alignment with NEP 2020 and its focus on equitable access, foundational literacy and numeracy, inclusion, teacher education, and vocational education.

pib.headline: Shri Dharmendra Pradhan hails Budget 2024-25 as pivotal milestone on India's path to becoming a developed nation by 2047
pib.summary: The Union Education Minister highlighted increased education-related allocations in the Union Budget 2024-25, including additional funding for Samagra Shiksha. The release presents the allocation as part of broader efforts to improve access to education, skilling, employment, and human-capital development.

pib.headline: Accessibility and Inclusivity in Education for Divyangs
pib.summary: The Ministry of Education explains that Samagra Shiksha includes a dedicated inclusive-education component for children with special needs. Support includes assessment, assistive devices, transportation, Braille and large-print materials, stipends for girls with special needs, therapeutic interventions, and barrier-free school infrastructure.

pib.headline: Quality Education
pib.summary: The Ministry of Education states that Samagra Shiksha supports quality and inclusive education for children from pre-school to Class 12. It provides assistance for school grants, uniforms and textbooks, ICT initiatives, remedial teaching, KGBVs, residential schools, hostels, and support for children with special needs.

pib.headline: Year End Review 2024: Department of School Education & Literacy
pib.summary: The Ministry of Education reports Samagra Shiksha achievements from 2018-19 through 2024-25, including school upgrades, strengthened schools, ICT and digital initiatives, vocational-education coverage, KGBV upgrades, and construction of girls’ toilets. The scheme continues to support universalization of school education from pre-primary through Class 12.

pib.headline: Union Education Minister lauds historic Budget 2025-26
pib.summary: The Ministry of Education states that the Union Budget 2025-26 increased the allocation for Samagra Shiksha compared with the 2024-25 revised estimate. The release places the increase within a wider expansion of education, connectivity, innovation, and school infrastructure initiatives.

cag.finding: The utilisation of funds ranged between 44 and 50 per cent under the Samagra Shiksha Scheme.
cag.parameter: Samagra Shiksha fund utilisation
cag.actual: Fund utilisation ranged between 44 and 50 per cent

cag.finding: Savings of ₹1,300 crore, representing 84.20 per cent of the net grant, occurred under the scheme Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (Elementary Education) (Central Share).
cag.parameter: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan central-share expenditure
cag.actual: ₹1,300 crore remained unspent, equal to 84.20 per cent of the net grant

cag.finding: Major components of Samagra Shiksha were not implemented in the test-checked districts for want of funds. Strengthening of existing schools was not undertaken in Bankura during 2019-20 to 2023-24, in Uttar Dinajpur during 2020-21 to 2023-24, in Murshidabad during 2020-21 and 2023-24, and in Dakshin Dinajpur during 2019-20 to 2021-22.
cag.parameter: Implementation of Samagra Shiksha components
cag.actual: Strengthening of existing schools was not implemented during the stated periods in four test-checked districts for want of funds

verdict.name: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan
verdict.summary: Accountability concerns: 1 critical and 2 major findings indicate the scheme is not meeting its stated objectives.

scheme.name: Bharatmala Pariyojana
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
scheme.description: Umbrella programme for highways development focusing on optimising efficiency of freight and passenger movement across India through development of Economic Corridors.
scheme.goals: Develop 34,800 km of national highways including 9,000 km of Economic Corridors. Complete by 2022 at cost of Rs 5.35 lakh crore.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: All highway users; logistics sector; connect 550 districts

pib.headline: Bharatmala Phase I: Rs 5.35 lakh crore, 34,800 km to be built by 2022
pib.summary: Ministry announces full Phase I target of 34,800 km to be completed by 2022 at approved cost of Rs 5.35 lakh crore.

pib.headline: Bharatmala: 11,000 km of National Highways awarded in FY22
pib.summary: NHAI announces 11,000 km of national highways awarded in FY22 under Bharatmala. Total 23,000 km awarded since inception.

pib.headline: Bharatmala Pariyojana
pib.summary: Under Phase-I of Bharatmala Pariyojana, 34,800 km of National Highway length was planned for development. By December 2023, 26,418 km had been awarded and about 15,549 km had been completed; projects in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana were also reported at bidding or awarded stages.

pib.headline: BHARATMALA PARIYOJANA
pib.summary: The release states that Bharatmala Pariyojana projects cover economic corridors, inter-corridors, feeder routes, national corridor efficiency improvements, border and international connectivity, coastal and port connectivity, and expressways. It also says the programme is intended to improve connectivity and reduce logistics costs, with progress monitored through regular reviews.

pib.headline: IMPACT OF BHARATMALA PARIYOJANA
pib.summary: Bharatmala Pariyojana was approved to develop 34,800 km of roads at an estimated cost of Rs. 5.35 lakh crore to improve connectivity and reduce logistics costs. As of October 31, 2024, projects covering 26,425 km had been awarded and 18,714 km had been constructed; an IIM Bangalore study on the programme's socioeconomic impact was under way.

pib.headline: Parliament Question: - Status of Ambitious Bharatmala Pariyojana
pib.summary: The release reports progress under Phase-I of Bharatmala Pariyojana, which covers 34,800 km. As of October 31, 2024, projects covering 26,425 km had been awarded and 18,714 km had been constructed; expenditure by NHAI under the programme reached Rs. 4.72 lakh crore up to November 30, 2024.

pib.headline: IMPLEMENTATION OF BHARATMALA PARIYOJAN
pib.summary: The release states that 26,425 km of Bharatmala Pariyojana projects had been awarded as of February 28, 2025, of which 19,826 km had been constructed. It also reports that 6,669 km of high-speed greenfield corridors had been awarded and 4,610 km completed, alongside the adoption of technologies such as LIDAR, drones, and automated machine-aided construction.

cag.finding: CAG found only 7,662 km of the 34,800 km Phase I target was completed by June 2023, against the 2022 deadline. Project cost has escalated to Rs 10.64 lakh crore, nearly double the original Rs 5.35 lakh crore estimate.
cag.parameter: Construction progress vs targets

cag.finding: CAG found land acquisition was pending for 28% of project length. Rs 1.1 lakh crore paid to NHAI via market borrowings had created debt burden with annual interest of Rs 18,000 crore, raising sustainability concerns.
cag.parameter: Land acquisition delays
cag.actual: 28 percent land still unacquired

verdict.name: Bharatmala Pariyojana
verdict.summary: Accountability concerns: 1 critical and 1 major finding indicate the scheme is not meeting its stated objectives.

scheme.name: POSHAN Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission)
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
scheme.description: Government's flagship programme to improve nutritional outcomes for children, pregnant women and lactating mothers. Uses technology and Jan Andolan approach.
scheme.goals: Reduce stunting from 38.4% to 25% by 2022. Reduce undernutrition from 35.7% to 20%. Reduce anaemia among children from 58.5% to 40%. Reduce low birth weight by 2%.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Children 0-6 years, pregnant women, lactating mothers across India

pib.headline: POSHAN Abhiyaan: Stunting reduced from 38.4% to 35.5% in 3 years
pib.summary: Women & Child Ministry claims stunting reduced from 38.4% to 35.5% citing POSHAN interventions as key driver.

pib.headline: Utilization of Funds Under POSHAN Abhiyaan
pib.summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development reported that, as of 31 March 2022, funds had been allocated to States and Union Territories under POSHAN Abhiyaan since the scheme’s launch in 2018. The release presented the financial utilization position of the programme.

pib.headline: 5th Poshan Pakhwada celebrations begin tomorrow
pib.summary: The Ministry announced that the fifth Poshan Pakhwada would be held from 20 March to 3 April 2023 nationwide. The campaign focused on popularising Shree Anna, holding Swasth Balak Spardha activities, and promoting Saksham Anganwadis through Jan Andolan and Jan Bhagidari.

pib.headline: MISSION POSHAN 2.0
pib.summary: The release described Mission POSHAN 2.0 as an integrated nutrition support programme building on POSHAN Abhiyaan. It highlighted improvements in nutrition quality and testing, technology-enabled monitoring through Poshan Tracker, diet diversity, food fortification, and promotion of millets.

pib.headline: Ministry of Women and Child Development celebrating the 6th Rashtriya Poshan Maah throughout September 2023
pib.summary: The Ministry announced the sixth Rashtriya Poshan Maah for September 2023 under the life-cycle approach of Mission Poshan 2.0. The campaign focused on improving awareness and action around nutrition during pregnancy, infancy, childhood, and adolescence under the theme of a nutrition-rich, educated, and empowered India.

pib.headline: Close to 10 lakh activities witnessed across the country on the 1st day of Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2023
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that the first day of Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2023 saw nearly 10 lakh activities nationwide. Activities included Mission LiFE nutrition initiatives, exclusive breastfeeding and complementary-feeding awareness, and other Jan Andolan efforts.

pib.headline: Poshan Utsav: Celebrating Nutrition to promote good nutrition behavior
pib.summary: The Ministry organized Poshan Utsav to promote good nutrition practices and highlight efforts to combat malnutrition. The event included the release of the Poshan Utsav Book and the announcement of a Cartoon Coalition to communicate nutrition messages to children.

pib.headline: Union Minister Smt Annpurna Devi launches 7th Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2024
pib.summary: The seventh Rashtriya Poshan Maah was launched in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, under Mission Poshan 2.0. Its focus themes included anaemia, growth monitoring, complementary feeding, Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi, technology for better governance, and the Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam initiative.

pib.headline: Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2024 emphasises consumption of balanced diet
pib.summary: The Ministry stated that the seventh Rashtriya Poshan Maah was promoting balanced diets and healthy nutrition practices. The campaign also addressed breastfeeding, complementary feeding, the first 1,000 days, sanitation, diarrhoea, and anaemia through community engagement and inter-ministerial collaboration.
pib.figureUnit: grams of fruit in the cited daily balanced-diet example

pib.headline: Smt. Annpurna Devi to grace closing ceremony of 7th Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2024 at Ranchi tomorrow
pib.summary: The Ministry announced the closing ceremony of the seventh Rashtriya Poshan Maah and reported that around 12 crore activities had been conducted by States and Union Territories during the campaign. The release also said that more than 11,000 Saksham Anganwadi Centres would be inaugurated virtually.

pib.headline: Year End Review: Achievements of Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, 2024
pib.summary: The Ministry’s year-end review reported progress under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, including digital nutrition monitoring through Poshan Tracker and community sensitisation activities. It stated that Poshan Tracker was tracking more than 10 crore beneficiaries and that over 30 crore community sensitisation activities were conducted in 2024.

cag.finding: The audit found non-coverage of a considerable percentage of targeted beneficiaries under POSHAN Abhiyaan in Odisha.
cag.parameter: Non-coverage of beneficiaries
cag.actual: 73 to 94 percent coverage
cag.reportExcerpt: Scrutiny revealed that the percentage of coverage of targeted beneficiaries under SNP ranged between 73 and 94 per cent during 2018-23.

cag.finding: A short delivery of wheat to Anganwadi Centres by the appointed Transport Agent was observed during the audit.
cag.parameter: Short delivery of wheat by Transport Agent
cag.reportExcerpt: Audit observed short delivery of 158 MT of wheat by Transport Agent during the period covered by audit.

cag.finding: Audit detected diversion of Take Home Ration (THR) funds for unrelated expenditure.
cag.parameter: Diversion of THR cost towards other expenditure
cag.claimed: THR funds to be used only for THR supply
cag.actual: THR cost diverted to excess payment for SHG charges
cag.reportExcerpt: Audit noticed diversion of THR cost amounting to ₹1.64 crore towards payment of processing and supervision charges to SHGs in excess of the admissible rates.

verdict.name: POSHAN Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission)
verdict.summary: Accountability concerns: 1 critical and 2 major findings indicate the scheme is not meeting its stated objectives.

scheme.name: PM Poshan Shakti Nirman (Mid-Day Meal Scheme)
scheme.description: Renamed from Mid-Day Meal Scheme, provides free hot cooked meals to students in government schools. Enhanced to include breakfast in aspirational districts.
scheme.goals: Provide nutritious meal to 11.80 crore school children daily. Improve enrollment, retention and attendance in schools. Address classroom hunger.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 11.80 crore students in government and government-aided schools

pib.headline: PM Poshan: 11.8 crore children fed daily in 11.2 lakh schools
pib.summary: Education Ministry announces PM Poshan scheme providing hot cooked meals to 11.8 crore children in government schools daily.

pib.headline: Government has approved the Centrally Sponsored Scheme ‘Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN)’ earlier known as ‘National Programme for Mid-Day Meal in Schools’
pib.summary: The release states that PM POSHAN provides hot cooked meals to eligible children in Government and Government-aided schools from 2021-22 to 2025-26. It also highlights additional features including Balvatika coverage, Tithi Bhojan, School Nutrition Gardens, mandatory social audits, locally sourced foods, and meal provision during disasters.

pib.headline: Enhancement of ‘Material Cost’ under the Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Scheme
pib.summary: The Ministry of Education enhanced PM POSHAN material costs by 13.70% with effect from December 1, 2024. Rates increased from ₹5.45 to ₹6.19 per meal for Balvatika and primary classes, and from ₹8.17 to ₹9.29 for upper-primary classes; the Centre will bear an additional ₹425.62 crore in 2024-25.

pib.headline: Enhancement of ‘Material Cost’ under the Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Scheme
pib.summary: The Ministry of Education announced a 9.50% enhancement in PM POSHAN material costs, applicable nationwide from May 1, 2025. The revised rates are ₹6.78 per student per day for Balvatika and primary classes and ₹10.17 for upper-primary classes, with an estimated additional central expenditure of ₹954 crore in 2025-26.

cag.finding: Enrolment of children in schools covered by the Mid-Day Meal Scheme declined consistently from 14.69 crore in 2009-10 to 13.87 crore in 2013-14; in contrast, private-school enrolment increased by 38 per cent from 4.02 crore to 5.53 crore.
cag.parameter: Enrolment in Mid-Day Meal Scheme-covered schools
cag.actual: Enrolment declined from 14.69 crore children in 2009-10 to 13.87 crore children in 2013-14.

verdict.name: PM Poshan Shakti Nirman (Mid-Day Meal Scheme)
verdict.summary: 1 major CAG finding indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (Phase III)
scheme.description: Provides all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations in rural areas. Phase III focuses on consolidation and upgradation of existing rural roads.
scheme.goals: Connect all remaining unconnected habitations of 500+ population. Upgrade 1,25,000 km of existing rural roads. Total road length: 2.5 lakh km.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Rural habitations with population over 500 (250 in hilly/tribal areas)

pib.headline: PMGSY Phase III: 1.25 lakh km roads to be upgraded for Rs 80,250 crore
pib.summary: Cabinet approves Phase III of PMGSY targeting upgradation of 1.25 lakh km existing rural roads to improve road quality.

pib.headline: PMGSY: 7.22 lakh km rural roads constructed since 2000
pib.summary: Rural Development Ministry announces 7.22 lakh km of rural roads constructed under PMGSY, connecting 99% of habitations over 500 population.

pib.headline: Development of Rural Roads
pib.summary: The release states that PMGSY-III was launched in 2019 to consolidate 1,25,000 km of Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations to markets, higher secondary schools and hospitals. As of July 21, 2022, 7,93,568 km of roads and 10,082 bridges had been sanctioned across PMGSY interventions, with 7,12,638 km of roads and 7,264 bridges completed.

pib.headline: Ministry of Rural Development announces Major Infrastructure Boost for State of Kerala
pib.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development sanctioned 33 roads measuring 159.86 km for Kerala under PMGSY-III. The projects involve an estimated investment of Rs. 160.56 crore and are intended to improve rural connectivity and access to markets, healthcare and education.

pib.headline: Ministry of Rural Development Announces Infrastructure Boost for North-Eastern Region with an estimated investment of Rs. 1,056.82 crore in Meghalaya under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana-III
pib.summary: The Ministry sanctioned 88 roads covering 782.155 km and 55 bridges under PMGSY-III for Meghalaya. The estimated investment is Rs. 1,056.82 crore, aimed at strengthening rural connectivity and access to essential services.

pib.headline: Ministry of Rural Development Announces Infrastructure Boost for North-Eastern Region with an estimated investment of Rs. 54.75 crore in Nagaland under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana-III
pib.summary: The Ministry sanctioned 55.89 km of road length under PMGSY-III for Nagaland. The projects carry an estimated investment of Rs. 54.75 crore and are intended to improve access to healthcare, education and markets in rural areas.

pib.headline: Infrastructure Developed under PMGSY-III
pib.summary: The release reports that 15,972 roads covering 1,22,419 km and 3,212 bridges had been sanctioned under PMGSY-III as of July 25, 2025. Of these, 11,727 roads covering 98,588 km and 1,373 bridges had been constructed across the country.

cag.finding: The Management’s decision not to upload Phase-I and Phase-II NITs on the PMGSY portal as prescribed in the Standard Bidding Document limited bidder participation: an average of two/three bidders participated in Phase-I and Phase-II, whereas six bidders participated in Phase-III.
cag.parameter: Tendering and bidder participation
cag.claimed: Two/three bidders participated on average in Phase-I and Phase-II
cag.actual: Six bidders participated in Phase-III

verdict.name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (Phase III)
verdict.summary: 1 major CAG finding indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
scheme.renamedFrom: Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
scheme.description: Mission to establish infrastructure to ensure basic services including water supply, sewerage, urban transport to households and build amenities in cities.
scheme.goals: Provide tap water connections to 1.06 crore urban households. Sewerage connections to 78 lakh households. Develop parks and green spaces.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 500 cities with population above 1 lakh

pib.headline: AMRUT 2.0 launched: All cities to get 100% water coverage
pib.summary: PM launches AMRUT 2.0 with target to provide 100% tap water coverage in all 4,700 statutory towns.

pib.headline: AMRUT: 139 lakh water connections provided, 80 lakh sewer connections
pib.summary: Ministry announces 139 lakh new water tap connections and 80 lakh sewer connections provided under AMRUT across 500 cities.

pib.headline: AMRUT focuses on development of infrastructure in the water sectors; States/UTs have taken up 5,850 projects worth ₹81,283 crore under AMRUT
pib.summary: The release states that AMRUT covers water supply, sewerage and septage management, storm-water drainage, non-motorized transport, and green spaces. States and Union Territories had taken up 5,850 projects worth ₹81,283 crore, with 4,158 projects completed and 126 lakh water tap and 95 lakh sewer connections provided.

pib.headline: AMRUT 2.0 aims to provide water supply through functional taps to all households in statutory towns and coverage of sewerage/septage management
pib.summary: AMRUT 2.0 is intended to provide universal functional tap-water coverage in all statutory towns and sewerage or septage-management coverage in the 500 cities covered under the first phase of AMRUT. The scheme has an indicative outlay of ₹2,99,000 crore, including a central outlay of ₹76,760 crore, for five years.

pib.headline: The Central allocation of ₹66,750 crore for AMRUT 2.0 projects has been distributed
pib.summary: The Ministry stated that the central allocation for AMRUT 2.0 projects had been distributed among States and Union Territories for the full mission period. Allocations were determined using an equitable formula based mainly on urban population and area.

pib.headline: STATUS OF AMRUT
pib.summary: The release reports that all State and Union Territory State Annual Action Plans under AMRUT had been approved for ₹77,640 crore, including ₹35,990 crore in committed central assistance. States and Union Territories had taken up 5,873 projects worth ₹82,222 crore, with 4,676 projects completed.

pib.headline: SUCCESS OF AMRUT
pib.summary: The release describes AMRUT as having been subsumed under AMRUT 2.0, while funding for ongoing and eligible AMRUT projects continued through March 2023. It reports approved State Annual Action Plans totaling ₹77,640 crore and notes that project implementation was monitored through Apex Committee reviews, independent monitoring agencies, and a dedicated portal.

pib.headline: STATUS OF AMRUT 2.0
pib.summary: AMRUT 2.0 extends the objective of universal water-supply coverage from 500 AMRUT cities to all statutory towns and focuses on water security and sewerage or septage management. State Water Action Plans covering 6,527 projects worth ₹1,29,636 crore had been approved, including plans for 148 lakh new tap connections and 33.42 lakh new sewer connections.

pib.headline: Planned development in Urban Areas
pib.summary: The release describes AMRUT’s GIS-based master-plan initiative for the 500 AMRUT cities, reporting final GIS databases for 443 towns and notified master plans for 180 towns. Under AMRUT 2.0, a GIS-based master-plan scheme was launched for Class-II towns and approved for 675 towns with an outlay of ₹631 crore.

pib.headline: IMPACT OF AMRUT ON INFRASTRUCTURE AND SERVICES
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that AMRUT had grounded 5,996 projects worth ₹83,345 crore, with works worth ₹77,691 crore physically executed. The mission had provided 189 lakh water tap connections and 149 lakh sewer connections, exceeding targets of 139 lakh and 145 lakh respectively.

pib.headline: SALIENT FEATURES OF AMRUT 2.0
pib.summary: The release states that AMRUT 2.0 had approved 8,998 projects worth ₹1,89,458.55 crore, including operations and maintenance costs. Contracts had been awarded for 4,916 projects worth ₹85,114.01 crore, while ₹11,756.13 crore in central assistance had been released to States and Union Territories.

pib.headline: Gender Equality And Empowerment Of Women For Urban Planning
pib.summary: The release reports the use of SCADA and other smart technologies in AMRUT water-supply and sewerage projects, including implementation in 230 water-supply and 146 sewerage projects. It also states that 57,134 functionaries had been trained under AMRUT against a target of 45,000, and highlights the AMRUT Mitra initiative involving women’s self-help groups.

pib.headline: UPGRADATION OF STPs
pib.summary: Under AMRUT, 890 sewerage and septage-management projects worth ₹34,505 crore had been grounded, creating or augmenting 4,447 MLD of sewage-treatment capacity, including 1,437 MLD for recycling or reuse. Under AMRUT 2.0, 592 projects worth ₹67,607.67 crore had been approved, covering 6,739 MLD of treatment capacity.

cag.finding: The State Urban Development Agency reported that Mission cities had achieved 36-37 reform milestones, whereas Audit found that only 15-16 milestones had actually been achieved.
cag.parameter: AMRUT reform milestones achieved
cag.actual: 15-16 milestones

cag.finding: Although the primary objective of AMRUT was universal coverage in water supply, none of the nine mission cities achieved this objective as of October 2024. Household water-supply coverage ranged from 9.39 per cent to 89.16 per cent.
cag.parameter: Household water-supply coverage
cag.actual: 9.39% to 89.16% across the nine mission cities; none achieved universal coverage

verdict.name: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)
verdict.summary: 2 major CAG findings indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: National Health Mission
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
scheme.description: Umbrella mission encompassing National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and National Urban Health Mission (NUHM). Continued and expanded under BJP government.
scheme.goals: Reduce Infant Mortality Rate to 25 per 1,000 live births. Maternal Mortality Ratio to 100 per lakh. Total Fertility Rate to 2.1. Universal immunization coverage.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: All rural and urban populations with focus on 18 high-focus states

pib.headline: 1.5 lakh Health and Wellness Centres operational under NHM/Ayushman Bharat
pib.summary: Ministry announces 1.5 lakh Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres operational, providing comprehensive primary health care.

pib.headline: NHM: Infant Mortality Rate falls to 28 per 1,000 live births
pib.summary: Health Ministry announces IMR has reduced to 28 per 1,000 live births from 37 in 2014, attributing progress to NHM interventions.

pib.headline: Update on Strengthening The Healthcare System
pib.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare described National Health Mission support for strengthening state and Union Territory public healthcare systems. As of July 24, 2023, 160,480 Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres had been operationalized to provide comprehensive primary healthcare.
pib.figureUnit: Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres

pib.headline: Health Ministry Releases "Health Dynamics of India (Infrastructure and Human Resources) 2022-23"
pib.summary: The Health Ministry released the annual Health Dynamics of India publication, formerly known as Rural Health Statistics. The publication provides state-wise information on healthcare infrastructure and human resources relevant to the National Health Mission and is intended to support planning, monitoring and policy decisions.

pib.headline: Update on National Health Mission
pib.summary: The release outlines National Health Mission support for public healthcare systems through initiatives including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, ambulance services, mobile medical units, ASHAs, dialysis and immunization programs. It reports reductions in maternal mortality, infant mortality and total fertility, along with 36.16 crore Ayushman Cards created as of December 12, 2024.

pib.headline: Achievements under National Health Mission (2021-24): A Milestone in Improving India’s Public Health Outcomes
pib.summary: The Ministry reported substantial progress under the National Health Mission during financial years 2021-22 through 2023-24. NHM engaged more than 12 lakh additional healthcare workers, supported 220 crore COVID-19 vaccine doses and contributed to improvements in maternal and child health, disease control and healthcare infrastructure.

pib.headline: Update on Status of Healthcare Infrastructure under NHM
pib.summary: The release describes the extension of the National Health Mission for financial years 2021-22 through 2025-26 and reports progress against its health-system targets. It states that 176,325 Ayushman Arogya Mandirs had been operationalized as of January 31, 2025, while full immunization coverage reached 93.6% as of October 31, 2024.

scheme.name: Khelo India Programme
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
scheme.description: Programme to revive sports culture at grassroots level in India. Identifies and trains talented young athletes with scholarships and world-class training.
scheme.goals: Identify 1,000 talented young athletes annually. Provide Rs 5 lakh/year scholarship for 8 years. Develop sports infrastructure across India.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Young athletes aged 8-18 identified through Khelo India Games

pib.headline: Khelo India: 2,500 athletes identified with Rs 5 lakh/year scholarship
pib.summary: Sports Ministry announces 2,500 talented young athletes receiving Rs 5 lakh annual scholarship under Khelo India for world-class training.

pib.headline: Year End Review: Events organized under the Khelo India Scheme
pib.summary: The Department of Sports reported that the fourth Khelo India Youth Games and the second Khelo India University Games had been organized successfully. It also noted approval of the Khelo India Scheme for continuation through the 15th Finance Commission cycle from 2021-22 to 2025-26.

pib.headline: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports receives Budget allocation of Rs. 3397.32 crore for FY 2023-24, with an increase of 11% over FY 2022-23; substantial increase in budget outlay for Khelo India
pib.summary: The Ministry received a budget allocation of Rs. 3397.32 crore for FY 2023-24, representing an 11% increase over the previous year. The allocation for the Khelo India programme was increased to Rs. 1000 crore.

pib.headline: Khelo India Dus Ka Dum tournament to be organized in 10 cities to celebrate International Women’s Day
pib.summary: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced the Khelo India Dus Ka Dum tournament as a women-focused sports initiative. The tournament was scheduled to be held in 10 cities from March 10 to 31, 2023.

pib.headline: First-ever Khelo India Para Games 2023 logo and mascot Ujjwala launched
pib.summary: The Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports launched the logo and mascot Ujjwala for the inaugural Khelo India Para Games. The release said the event would expand the Khelo India platform to identify and support talented para athletes.

pib.headline: Union Minister Shri Anurag Singh Thakur to inaugurate first-ever Khelo India Para Games 2023
pib.summary: The inaugural Khelo India Para Games were scheduled in New Delhi from December 10 to 17, 2023. More than 1400 players from 32 states and Union Territories and the Services Sports Board were set to compete across seven para-sport disciplines.

pib.headline: Over Rs. 30.83 crore released to Khelo India Athletes in 2023-24 under scholarship scheme
pib.summary: The Sports Authority of India released Rs. 30.83 crore to Khelo India Athletes during 2023-24, including the fourth-quarter out-of-pocket allowance for 2571 athletes. The release stated that close to 3000 athletes receive support for training, coaching, diet, equipment, medical insurance and allowances.

pib.headline: Promoting sports talent in small towns through various government schemes
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that the Khelo India Scheme was supporting 32 State Centres of Excellence and 1059 Khelo India Centres, with 302 accredited academies. It also stated that 2737 athletes had been identified and that each identified sportsperson could receive financial assistance of Rs. 6.28 lakh per year.

pib.headline: Khelo India's role in boosting India's Olympic and Asian Games performance
pib.summary: The Ministry said 124 Khelo India Athletes were part of India’s 2022 Asian Games contingent and contributed 42 of the country’s 106 medals. It also reported that 28 Khelo India Athletes were included in India’s 117-member Paris 2024 Olympic contingent.

pib.headline: Promotion of sports through Khelo India Scheme
pib.summary: The Ministry stated that the Khelo India Scheme had been extended for five years from 2021-22 to 2025-26 and described its five components covering infrastructure, competitions and talent development, centres and academies, the Fit India Movement, and inclusiveness through sports. It reported that Khelo India Athletes had set 5939 national and 1424 international records in the past two years and the current year.

pib.headline: Implementation of Khelo India Scheme
pib.summary: The Ministry reported approval of 323 new sports infrastructure projects with a sanctioned cost of Rs. 3073.97 crore. It also reported 1041 Khelo India Centres, 32 State Centres of Excellence, 301 accredited academies and 2781 Khelo India Athletes receiving programme support.

pib.headline: Impact of Khelo India Scheme
pib.summary: The Ministry stated that the Khelo India Scheme supported athletes across 21 sports, including para-athletics, through coaching, equipment, medical care and monthly allowances. It reported that 2781 Khelo India Athletes had been identified, including 124 who contributed 42 medals at the 2022 Asian Games and 28 who were part of India’s Paris 2024 Olympic contingent.

cag.finding: Government of India directly transferred ₹5.70 crore to the Nagaland State Sports Council under the Khelo India National Programme during 2019-20.
