scheme.name: Mission Indradhanush
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
scheme.description: Immunisation programme to cover all children under 2 years and pregnant women who are either unvaccinated or partially vaccinated against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases.
scheme.goals: Achieve full immunisation coverage for at least 90% children by 2020 across all districts. Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) to cover 190 low-coverage districts.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Children under 2 years and pregnant women across India

pib.headline: IMI 4.0: 97% immunization coverage claimed in target districts
pib.summary: Health Ministry announces Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 has achieved 97% full immunization coverage in 416 districts.

pib.headline: Focus on Universal Immunization: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya launches Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) 4.0
pib.summary: The Union Health Minister launched Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 to cover partially vaccinated and unvaccinated children and pregnant women. The campaign was planned in three rounds across 416 districts in 33 States and Union Territories.

pib.headline: Update on Mission Indradhanush
pib.summary: The release reports that Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 was conducted in 416 high-focus districts during 2022. It also states that six States or Union Territories achieved 100% full immunization coverage and 17 States achieved coverage above 90% under HMIS 2022-23.

pib.headline: Intensified Mission Indradhanush 5.0 campaign with special focus on improvement of Measles and Rubella vaccination coverage will conclude all three rounds on 14 October 2023
pib.summary: The release says IMI 5.0 was being conducted across all districts for the first time and expanded eligibility to children up to five years of age. During the first two rounds, more than 34.69 lakh children and 6.55 lakh pregnant women had received vaccine doses as of September 30, 2023.

pib.headline: Myth vs. Facts: Media reports highlighting high number of zero-dose children in India paint an incomplete picture of India’s immunization efforts
pib.summary: The release states that 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women had been vaccinated under Mission Indradhanush through 2023. It also reports that full immunization coverage for the country was 93.23% in FY 2023-24.

pib.headline: Update on Mission Indradhanush: More than 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women have been vaccinated in all phases of Mission Indradhanush conducted so far
pib.summary: The release describes Mission Indradhanush as a catch-up vaccination campaign for children and pregnant women missed by routine immunization services. It reports that 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women had been vaccinated across all phases conducted in the country.

cag.finding: In the exit conference, the Principal Secretary stated that Mission Indradhanush was conducted in high- and medium-priority districts to close immunisation gaps during 2015-16 and 2016-17.
cag.parameter: Mission Indradhanush implementation and immunisation-gap closure

cag.finding: The State had achieved the target of 100 per cent immunisation of children in the 0-1 year age group, including coverage of dropout children through Mission Indradhanush.
cag.parameter: Immunisation coverage of children aged 0-1 years

verdict.name: Mission Indradhanush
verdict.summary: Only minor issues found. The scheme is broadly meeting its stated objectives per available CAG audits.

scheme.name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme
scheme.description: Scheme to give companies incentives on incremental sales from products manufactured in India over a base year. Covers 14 key sectors including electronics, pharma, autos.
scheme.goals: Boost domestic manufacturing. Attract Rs 2 lakh crore investment over 5 years. Create 60 lakh employment. Generate Rs 30 lakh crore in production.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Manufacturers in 14 identified sectors

pib.headline: PLI Schemes: Rs 47,500 crore investment committed, 3 lakh jobs created
pib.summary: Commerce Ministry announces PLI beneficiaries have committed Rs 47,500 crore investment and created over 3 lakh direct employment.

pib.headline: Production Linked Incentive Schemes for 14 key sectors aim to enhance India’s manufacturing capabilities and exports
pib.summary: The press release states that PLI schemes covering 14 key sectors were announced with an outlay of Rs. 1.97 lakh crore to strengthen manufacturing capabilities and exports. It notes that 733 applications had been selected, including 176 MSMEs, and that the schemes were expected to attract investment, improve efficiency and create employment.

pib.headline: Scaling New Heights: How the PLI Scheme is Reshaping Industries
pib.summary: The release reports that, as of August 2024, PLI schemes across 14 sectors had attracted Rs. 1.46 lakh crore in investment, generating incremental production or sales of more than Rs. 12.50 lakh crore. It also reports employment of over 9.5 lakh people, exports exceeding Rs. 4 lakh crore and 764 approved applications.

pib.headline: PLI scheme incentivizes domestic manufacturing, increases production, creates new jobs and boosts exports
pib.summary: The release reports that PLI schemes across 14 sectors had generated Rs. 1.61 lakh crore in investment, Rs. 14 lakh crore in production and Rs. 5.31 lakh crore in exports. It also states that the schemes had generated 11.5 lakh jobs, with 764 applications approved and 176 MSME beneficiaries.

verdict.name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme
verdict.summary: No CAG audit findings are available for this scheme yet.

scheme.name: PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
scheme.description: Micro-credit scheme for street vendors to help them resume livelihoods after COVID-19 lockdowns. Provides collateral-free working capital loans with incentives for digital transactions.
scheme.goals: Provide Rs 10,000 initial working capital loan to 50 lakh street vendors. Subsequent loans of Rs 20,000 and Rs 50,000 on timely repayment.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 50 lakh street vendors affected by COVID-19 lockdowns

pib.headline: PM SVANidhi: 40.6 lakh street vendors given loans worth Rs 4,459 crore
pib.summary: MoHUA announces 40.6 lakh loans disbursed to street vendors under PM SVANidhi. 25.8 lakh vendors adopted digital payments.

pib.headline: PM acknowledges transformative impact of PM SVANidhi
pib.summary: The Prime Minister highlighted State Bank of India research describing PM SVANidhi as financially empowering and inclusive. The research noted the scheme’s role in supporting women and marginalized street vendors through formal credit.

pib.headline: PM-SVANidhi promoting inclusive entrepreneurship
pib.summary: The release reported that PM-SVANidhi had disbursed ₹9,152 crore in loans and promoted inclusive entrepreneurship among street vendors. It also described repayment and progression patterns across the scheme’s three loan tranches.

pib.headline: PM SVANIDHI with enhanced loans from banks, and UPI linked credit cards with ₹30,000 limit
pib.summary: The Union Budget 2025-26 proposed enhanced bank loans under PM SVANidhi and UPI-linked credit cards for street vendors. The credit cards were announced with a limit of up to ₹30,000.

pib.headline: Cabinet approves restructuring and extension of lending period beyond 31.12.2024 of PM Street Vendors AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved restructuring PM SVANidhi and extending its lending period until March 31, 2030. The restructured scheme includes higher loan amounts, UPI-linked RuPay credit cards, digital cashback incentives, and broader socio-economic support for vendors and their families.

pib.headline: Union Minister reviews progress of PM SVANidhi Scheme with States, UTs and Banks
pib.summary: The Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs reviewed implementation of PM SVANidhi with representatives of States, Union Territories, banks, and related departments. The review reaffirmed the government’s focus on timely credit delivery and effective implementation through the banking and local-government systems.

pib.headline: SVANidhi: Empowering Street Vendors
pib.summary: The backgrounder described the restructured PM SVANidhi scheme, including its extended lending period through March 2030 and enhanced credit facilities. It stated that the scheme aims to benefit 1.15 crore street vendors, including 50 lakh new beneficiaries.

verdict.name: PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
verdict.summary: No CAG audit findings are available for this scheme yet.

scheme.name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
scheme.description: Skill training and placement programme for rural youth from poor families. Aims to diversify incomes of rural families and cater to career aspirations of rural youth.
scheme.goals: Skill and place 10 lakh rural youth by 2017. Achieve 75% placement in jobs post training. Cover all 676 districts across India.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Rural youth aged 15-35 from poor families across India

pib.headline: DDU-GKY: 10.5 lakh rural youth trained and placed since 2014
pib.summary: Rural Development Ministry announces over 10.5 lakh rural youth have been trained and placed in jobs under DDU-GKY scheme.

pib.headline: Rural development Secretary chairs a webinar on Captive Employment Policy under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
pib.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development held a webinar to promote the DDU-GKY Captive Employer initiative, which links industry demand with training and assured placement for rural poor youth. More than 16 Sector Skill Councils and over 180 stakeholders participated.

pib.headline: Deen Dayal Upadhyay-Grameen Kaushal Yojana in North Eastern Region
pib.summary: The release describes DDU-GKY as a placement-linked skilling programme for rural poor youth aged 15–35 in the North Eastern Region. It notes the scheme’s inclusion provisions, including earmarking 50% of funds for SCs and STs and 15% for minorities.
pib.figureUnit: funds earmarked for SCs and STs

pib.headline: Review of Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY): More than 7 lakh candidates placed from 2014-15
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that more than 7 lakh candidates had been placed under DDU-GKY since 2014-15, with 1.28 lakh candidates undergoing training at the time of the release. For 2021-22, the programme targeted training 2.80 lakh candidates and placing 1.96 lakh.

pib.headline: Big boost to rural employment as more than 31,000 jobs on the way under DDU-GKY
pib.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development announced MoUs with 19 captive employers under the Recruit, Train and Deploy model. The employers were given a target to train and provide gainful employment to 31,067 rural poor youths, with a minimum salary of ₹10,000 per month for at least six months.

pib.headline: Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh initiates ‘Captive Employment’ initiative under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY), paving the way for greater industry participation in skilling rural poor youth
pib.summary: The Minister onboarded 19 captive employers under DDU-GKY to train rural poor youth and provide employment in their own establishments or subsidiaries. The first phase was intended to train and place more than 31,000 rural youth.

pib.headline: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY): Empowering Rural Youth and Fostering Inclusive Development
pib.summary: The release states that DDU-GKY had trained 14.51 lakh candidates and placed 8.70 lakh candidates since inception, based on data through May 31, 2023. It also reports that ₹7,015.61 crore had been released under the programme through April 30, 2023.

pib.headline: Beneficiaries under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana - DDU-GKY
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that 16,90,046 candidates had been trained and 10,97,265 placed under DDU-GKY from FY 2014-15 through November 2024. It stated that 65% of candidates had secured gainful employment after completing training and outlined enhanced provisions under DDU-GKY 2.0.

pib.headline: Role of NRLM in Enhancing Skill Development and Employment Opportunities
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that DDU-GKY had trained 17,50,784 candidates and placed 11,48,247 candidates since inception through June 2025. The release also describes DDU-GKY as a placement-linked programme for rural poor youth aged 15–35, with jobs intended to provide regular wages at or above minimum wages.

cag.finding: ORMAS received ₹657.90 crore under DDU-GKY during 2014-19 and utilised ₹568.43 crore, representing 86 per cent utilisation as of March 2019.
cag.parameter: DDU-GKY fund utilisation
cag.actual: ₹568.43 crore utilised

cag.finding: The Punarjani skilling and placement project targeted training for 5,000 Kudumbashree workers but benefited only 1,794 members; the audit also found that Programme Implementation Agencies were not monitored by Kudumbashree, resulting in deficiencies in the scheme.
cag.parameter: DDU-GKY-related skilling and placement outcomes
cag.actual: 1,794 members benefited

cag.finding: The subject-specific compliance audit on implementation of DDU-GKY found irregularities in the selection of project implementing agencies and awarding of projects, as well as irregularities in the conduct of training and placement.
cag.parameter: Project-implementing-agency selection, project awards, training and placement

verdict.name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
verdict.summary: 2 major CAG findings indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: Atal Bhujal Yojana
scheme.description: Scheme for sustainable groundwater management with community participation in water-stressed areas. Focuses on demand-side interventions and community behaviour change.
scheme.goals: Improve groundwater management in 8,353 water-stressed gram panchayats across 7 states. Reduce groundwater extraction by 20%. Increase community participation.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 8,353 gram panchayats in Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, UP

pib.headline: Atal Bhujal Yojana: Water security plans prepared for 8,353 gram panchayats
pib.summary: Jal Shakti Ministry announces Water Security Plans prepared for all 8,353 gram panchayats in 7 states under Atal Bhujal, with community-led groundwater conservation underway.

pib.headline: Groundwater extraction reduced by 18% in Atal Bhujal districts since 2020
pib.summary: Ministry claims groundwater extraction rate has reduced by 18% across 8,353 programme gram panchayats due to behaviour change, micro-irrigation, and recharge structures.

pib.headline: Atal Bhujal Yojana and Jal Jeevan Mission
pib.summary: Atal Bhujal Yojana is being implemented in water-stressed Gram Panchayats across 229 administrative blocks or talukas in 80 districts of seven states. The release states that Rs. 1,688.90 crore had been released to the participating states as of July 12, 2023, with implementation based on community participation and performance indicators.

pib.headline: Implementation of Atal Bhujal Yojana
pib.summary: The scheme is being implemented in 8,203 water-stressed Gram Panchayats across 80 districts in seven states through a community-led approach to sustainable groundwater management. The release reports that around 81,000 supply-side structures were constructed or renovated and approximately 9 lakh hectares were brought under efficient water-use practices.

pib.headline: Implementation and Expansion of Atal Bhujal Yojana
pib.summary: The release reports progress under the community-led groundwater management scheme, including public disclosure of groundwater data and preparation of Water Budgets and Water Security Plans across all 8,203 participating Gram Panchayats. Around 81,700 supply-side structures were constructed or renovated, and about 9 lakh hectares were brought under efficient water-use practices.

pib.headline: Expansion of Atal Bhujal Yojana
pib.summary: Atal Bhujal Yojana is being implemented in seven states and benefits 8,203 water-stressed Gram Panchayats through demand- and supply-side groundwater interventions. From October 2021 to December 2024, around 9.78 lakh beneficiaries received assistance or subsidies for efficient water-use practices, while approximately 81,700 water-conservation and groundwater-recharge structures were constructed or renovated.

pib.headline: Coverage under Atal Bhujal Yojana
pib.summary: Atal Bhujal Yojana was implemented as a pilot scheme across 8,203 priority water-stressed Gram Panchayats in seven states. Its stated objective was to improve groundwater management through community participation, demand-side interventions, stronger local institutions, and incentives for groundwater conservation.

verdict.name: Atal Bhujal Yojana
verdict.summary: No CAG audit findings are available for this scheme yet.

scheme.name: PM Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM KUSUM)
scheme.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
scheme.description: Scheme to add solar power generation capacity in rural areas, solarise agricultural pump sets, and install grid-connected solar power plants for farmers.
scheme.goals: Install 30.8 GW solar capacity through 3 components: standalone solar pumps, solarisation of existing pumps, and solar plants on barren land. Cover 35 lakh farmers by 2022.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 35 lakh farmers with agricultural pump sets

pib.headline: PM KUSUM: 3 lakh solar pumps installed, 2,500 MW capacity added
pib.summary: MNRE announces 3 lakh solar pumps installed for farmers under PM KUSUM. Solar capacity of 2,500 MW added from Component A and B.

pib.headline: Steps by MNRE to implement PM-KUSUM scheme
pib.summary: The Ministry described implementation measures for PM-KUSUM, including extending the scheme through 31 March 2026 and increasing eligible pump capacity for certain farmers from 7.5 HP to 15 HP. The scheme targets 30.8 GW of solar capacity addition with total central financial support of ₹34,422 crore.

pib.headline: PM-KUSUM - Grid-connected solar power plants of 89.45 MW capacity installed; 2.09 lakh agriculture pumps have been solarized
pib.summary: As of 28 February 2023, 89.45 MW of grid-connected solar power plants had been installed and 2.09 lakh agriculture pumps had been solarized under PM-KUSUM. The reported installations were estimated to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 0.67 million tonnes and diesel consumption by 143 million litres annually.

pib.headline: 2,08,648 farmers have benefitted from PM-KUSUM scheme
pib.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy reported that 2,08,648 farmers had benefited from the PM-KUSUM scheme. The release described the scheme's implementation and support for solar pumps and solarization of agricultural pumps.

pib.headline: Availability of low-cost financing for farmers and state share of funds is a major challenge in implementation of the PM-KUSUM Scheme
pib.summary: The release outlined PM-KUSUM targets of 10 GW under Component A, 20 lakh standalone solar water pumps under Component B, and solarization of 15 lakh existing grid-connected agricultural pumps under Component C. As of 30 June 2023, 113.08 MW had been installed under Component A and about 2.45 lakh pumps had been installed or solarized under Components B and C combined.

pib.headline: Progress of Implementation of PM-KUSUM Yojana
pib.summary: The release stated that PM-KUSUM targets 30.8 GW of solar capacity addition by 31 March 2026, supported by ₹34,422 crore in central financial assistance. Its components include 10,000 MW of decentralized solar plants, 20 lakh standalone solar pumps, and solarization of 15 lakh grid-connected agricultural pumps.

pib.headline: Major ongoing Renewable Energy Schemes and Programmes
pib.summary: The Ministry listed PM-KUSUM among its major ongoing renewable energy programmes. The scheme promotes small grid-connected solar power plants, standalone solar agricultural pumps, and solarization of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps, benefiting farmers, states, and distribution companies.

pib.headline: PM-KUSUM SCHEME
pib.summary: The release described the three PM-KUSUM components: decentralized solar power plants, standalone solar agricultural pumps, and solarization of grid-connected agricultural pumps. As of 30 June 2024, 4,11,222 farmers had benefited from the scheme nationwide, including 51,097 farmers in Uttar Pradesh according to state-provided information.

pib.headline: GST on Renewable Energy Devices Rationalised to 5% to Accelerate India’s Clean Energy Transition; Farmers under PM-KUSUM to Save ₹1,750 Crore on 10 Lakh Solar Pumps with GST Cut
pib.summary: The release said the GST reduction on renewable-energy devices would lower the cost of PM-KUSUM solar pumps. It estimated that a 5 HP solar pump would become cheaper by nearly ₹17,500 and that farmers could collectively save ₹1,750 crore across 10 lakh pumps.

pib.headline: PM-KUSUM Registers Significant Progress: 10,203 MW Installed and ₹7,106 Crore Released Till November 2025
pib.summary: As of 30 November 2025, 10,203 MW had been installed under all components of PM-KUSUM and ₹7,106 crore had been released. The Ministry also reported revised implementation guidelines, priority for small and marginal farmers and micro-irrigation users, and outreach activities to expand the scheme.

pib.headline: PM-KUSUM Empowers Farmers as ‘Urjadata’, Reaching Over 20 Lakh Beneficiaries
pib.summary: The release reported that PM-KUSUM had reached more than 20 lakh beneficiaries and highlighted income opportunities from leasing land for solar plants. It stated that farmers could earn up to ₹80,000 per hectare per year from land leasing and save about ₹60,000 annually on diesel through solar pumps.

cag.finding: As of 31 March 2023, only 98.78 MW of solar power Power Purchase Agreements had been signed under Component A of PM-KUSUM against the State target of 500 MW, and only 3 MW had been commissioned, representing less than one per cent of the target achievement.
cag.parameter: PM-KUSUM Component A solar power capacity implementation
cag.actual: 3 MW commissioned

verdict.name: PM Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM KUSUM)
verdict.summary: 1 major CAG finding indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: Swamitva Scheme
scheme.description: Scheme to provide property rights to residents of rural areas of India by mapping land parcels using drone technology. Provides property cards to households.
scheme.goals: Survey and map 6.62 lakh villages by 2025. Issue property cards to all village household owners. Enable property-based credit in rural areas.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Residents of 6.62 lakh villages with houses in abadi areas

pib.headline: Swamitva: 1.25 crore property cards distributed in 3 lakh villages
pib.summary: PM distributes 1.25 crore property cards to rural households under Swamitva Scheme. 3 lakh villages surveyed using drones.

pib.headline: PROPERTY CARDS
pib.summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj reported that states had prepared 1.63 crore property cards under the SVAMITVA Scheme as of 6 December 2023. Drone surveys had been completed in 2,88,942 villages, and ₹354.52 crore had been released under the scheme.

pib.headline: Survey and Mapping with improvised Technology
pib.summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj stated that SVAMITVA uses drone technology to survey inhabited rural areas and provide household owners with legal property records. As of 19 July 2024, drone surveys had been completed in 3.12 lakh villages and 2.03 crore property cards had been prepared in 1.30 lakh villages.

pib.headline: Empowering Rural India
pib.summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj announced that 57 lakh SVAMITVA property cards would be distributed on 27 December 2024 across 46,351 villages in 10 states and two Union Territories. The release also reported that drone surveys had been completed in 3.17 lakh villages and 2.19 crore property cards had been prepared for nearly 1.49 lakh villages.

pib.headline: Empowering Rural India with Legal Land Ownership 65 Lakh SVAMITVA Property Cards Distributed
pib.summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj reported that 65 lakh SVAMITVA property cards were distributed across more than 50,000 villages in 10 states and two Union Territories on 18 January 2025. The cards provide rural property owners with records of rights intended to support access to credit, reduce disputes, and improve village planning.

pib.headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Distributes 65 lakh Property Cards under SVAMITVA Scheme; Total Property Cards Distributed Reach 2.25 Crore Milestone
pib.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi presided over the distribution of 65 lakh property cards under the Ministry of Panchayati Raj’s SVAMITVA Scheme. The distribution covered more than 50,000 villages across 10 states and two Union Territories, bringing the total number of distributed property cards to 2.25 crore.

pib.headline: Building a Self-Reliant India 5 Years of SVAMITVA Scheme
pib.summary: On the scheme’s fifth anniversary, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj reported that more than 2.42 crore property cards had been created for 1.61 lakh villages. Drone surveys had been completed in 3.20 lakh villages, covering an estimated 68,122 square kilometres.

verdict.name: Swamitva Scheme
verdict.summary: No CAG audit findings are available for this scheme yet.

scheme.name: PMAY (Gramin) – PM Awas Yojana Rural
scheme.description: Separate from PMAY Urban. Provides financial assistance to rural BPL households to construct pucca houses with basic amenities including toilet, LPG connection, electricity.
scheme.goals: Construct 2.95 crore pucca houses for rural poor by March 2022. Each house to have toilet, electricity, cooking gas. Unit cost Rs 1.20 lakh (plain) and Rs 1.30 lakh (hilly/tribal).
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Rural BPL households living in kaccha or dilapidated houses

pib.headline: PM: Every poor family will get a pucca house by 2022
pib.summary: PM announces from Red Fort that all remaining rural households will get a pucca house by 2022 under PMAY-Gramin, allocating Rs 1.30 lakh per house.

pib.headline: PMAY-G: 2.44 crore houses completed, largest rural housing push ever
pib.summary: Rural Development Ministry announces 2.44 crore pucca houses completed under PMAY-Gramin by March 2022, each with toilet, electricity and LPG connection.

pib.headline: Cabinet approves implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana–Gramin (PMAY-G) during FY 2024-25 to 2028-29
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of PMAY-G through FY 2028-29, including assistance for constructing two crore additional pucca houses with basic amenities. The approval carries a total outlay of ₹3,06,137 crore and is expected to benefit nearly 10 crore people.

pib.headline: Celebrating Awaas Diwas 2024: Empowering Rural India through Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin
pib.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development highlighted PMAY-G’s expansion by two crore additional houses for FY 2024-29, supported by a total outlay of ₹3,06,137 crore. The release also reported that 74% of sanctioned houses were owned solely or jointly by women and that nearly three lakh rural masons had been trained.

pib.headline: Automatic exclusion criteria for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin scheme beneficiaries
pib.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development described revised automatic-exclusion criteria for identifying beneficiaries in the new PMAY-G phase, including removal of exclusions related to motorized two-wheelers, fishing boats, landline phones and refrigerators. The monthly household-income exclusion threshold was increased from ₹10,000 to ₹15,000, while 3.21 crore houses had been sanctioned and more than 2.67 crore completed at the time of the release.

pib.headline: Achievement of targets under PMAY-G
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that all houses under the original 2.95-crore PMAY-G target had been sanctioned by March 31, 2024. As of February 2, 2025, States and Union Territories had received a cumulative target of 3.79 crore houses, with 3.34 crore sanctioned and 2.69 crore completed.

pib.headline: Transparency and Accountability under PMAY-G
pib.summary: The release explained that PMAY-G beneficiaries are identified using housing-deprivation parameters, exclusion criteria, Gram Sabha verification and an appellate process. It also described the Awaas+ 2024 app, which supports assisted and self-surveys, Aadhaar-based e-KYC, face authentication, geotagged photos and AI/ML-based monitoring.

pib.headline: Beneficiaries of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Rural)
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that PMAY-G had a cumulative target of 3.79 crore houses as of March 17, 2025, of which 3.56 crore had been sanctioned and 2.72 crore completed. The release also noted that at least 60% of targets are earmarked for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe households, subject to beneficiary availability and verification.

cag.finding: The failure to upload data pertaining to 7.15 lakh beneficiaries resulted in the Government of India refusing to include them in the Permanent Wait List, depriving them of a pucca house.
cag.parameter: Beneficiary identification and inclusion in the Permanent Wait List
cag.actual: 7.15 lakh beneficiaries were not included in the Permanent Wait List

cag.finding: Audit noted that 8.59 lakh eligible beneficiaries identified by Gram Sabhas were excluded from the Permanent Wait List, while 12.25 lakh beneficiaries could not be included in the list and were deprived of benefits under PMAY-G. The State also surrendered the target of 5.27 lakh houses due to non-availability of households in the Permanent Wait List.
cag.parameter: Beneficiary identification, Permanent Wait List and housing target achievement
cag.claimed: 5.27 lakh houses were allotted as a target
cag.actual: 8.59 lakh eligible beneficiaries were excluded; 12.25 lakh beneficiaries were not included; the 5.27 lakh-house target was surrendered

cag.finding: The State completed construction of 34.18 lakh PMAY-G houses by March 2024 out of 34.71 lakh houses sanctioned during 2016-17 to 2022-23; deficiencies were observed in implementation of the scheme.
cag.parameter: Construction completion of sanctioned PMAY-G houses
cag.actual: 34.18 lakh houses completed by March 2024

verdict.name: PMAY (Gramin) – PM Awas Yojana Rural
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 2 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: Aspirational Districts Programme
scheme.description: Programme to quickly and effectively transform the most underdeveloped districts of India across 5 thematic areas: health, education, agriculture, financial inclusion, and infrastructure.
scheme.goals: Convergence of central and state scheme spending. Improve rankings of 112 most backward districts by 2022. Real-time monitoring via Championsof Change dashboard.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 112 aspirational districts across 28 states

pib.headline: Delta Ranking: 25 districts in top performers across all 5 sectors
pib.summary: PM lauds 25 aspirational districts that feature in top performers across all 5 thematic areas — health & nutrition, education, agriculture, financial inclusion, and basic infrastructure.

pib.headline: Aspirational Districts: 112 districts show double-digit improvement in composite index
pib.summary: NITI Aayog announces 112 aspirational districts collectively improved composite development index by 16.1 points in 4 years across health, education, agriculture, and infrastructure.

pib.headline: Update on Aspirational District Program in targeted districts: Aspirational Districts have shown improvement with respect to the Health and Nutrition indicators
pib.summary: NITI Aayog reported that Aspirational Districts had generally improved on Health and Nutrition indicators. The programme uses convergence of existing schemes, monthly performance assessments, and challenge-based funding to address critical gaps.
pib.figureUnit: weightage assigned to Health and Nutrition

pib.headline: ‘Sampoornata Abhiyan’ launched by NITI Aayog to attain saturation in key social-sector indicators
pib.summary: NITI Aayog launched a three-month nationwide campaign to achieve 100% saturation of 12 key social-sector indicators in Aspirational Districts and Blocks. Launch events were organised across all 112 Aspirational Districts and 500 Aspirational Blocks, covering health, nutrition, agriculture, social development, and education.

pib.headline: Cabinet approves Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan
pib.summary: The Cabinet approved a mission aimed at saturation coverage of tribal-majority villages and tribal families, including villages in Aspirational Districts. The mission has a total outlay of ₹79,156 crore and is expected to cover around 63,000 villages benefiting more than 5 crore tribal people.

pib.headline: Namsai Climbs from 97th to 12th: A Success Story of Aspirational Districts Programme
pib.summary: The release highlighted Namsai district’s progress under the Aspirational Districts Programme, including its improvement from 97th to 12th place in rankings. It also cited 100% conversion of health centres and initiatives to improve maternal care, early childhood education, and school infrastructure.

cag.finding: Audit found that ₹442.18 crore was incurred by CPSEs in aspirational districts under the common theme, representing 11.78 per cent of total CSR expenditure, and that only 55 CPSEs incurred CSR expenditure in aspirational districts.
cag.parameter: Corporate Social Responsibility expenditure and participation in aspirational districts
cag.actual: ₹442.18 crore, or 11.78 per cent of total CSR expenditure, was incurred in aspirational districts; only 55 CPSEs incurred such expenditure.

cag.finding: The Board did not have the data points specified in the NITI Aayog Aspirational District indicator framework. CAG observed that, without the required data, evaluation of the outcomes of the Board's activities was not feasible and the Board could not demonstrate the effectiveness of its operations in measurable terms.
cag.parameter: Availability and use of NITI Aayog Aspirational District indicators for monitoring and evaluation
cag.actual: Required data points under the NITI Aayog Aspirational District indicator framework were not available with the Board, preventing measurable evaluation of outcomes.

cag.finding: The Cluster Facilitation Project, aimed at improving performance in aspirational districts, remained largely ineffective due to delays in operationalisation, under-deployment of Thematic Experts, and poor achievement of performance deliverables despite payment of ₹6.56 crore. Only 11 per cent of the Thematic Experts were appointed.
cag.parameter: Cluster Facilitation Project implementation and deployment of Thematic Experts
cag.actual: Only 11 per cent of Thematic Experts were appointed; the project remained largely ineffective despite payment of ₹6.56 crore.

verdict.name: Aspirational Districts Programme
verdict.summary: Accountability concerns: 1 critical and 2 major findings indicate the scheme is not meeting its stated objectives.

scheme.name: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
scheme.description: Scheme to promote apprenticeship training in India by sharing 25% of prescribed stipend with employers for fresh apprentices. Target: 50 lakh apprentices by 2020.
scheme.goals: Engage 50 lakh apprentices by March 2020. Share 25% of stipend (up to Rs 1,500/month) with employers. Make apprenticeship more attractive for industry.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Industry partners; unemployed youth seeking on-the-job training

pib.headline: Government targets 50 lakh apprentices by 2020 under NAPS
pib.summary: Ministry of Skill Development announces target to engage 50 lakh apprentices by March 2020 with industry through NAPS incentive of Rs 1,500/month stipend support.

pib.headline: NAPS: 9.7 lakh apprentices engaged, Rs 310 crore stipend support disbursed
pib.summary: Skill Ministry announces 9.7 lakh apprentices engaged under NAPS with Rs 310 crore disbursed as stipend support to employers since 2016.

pib.headline: MSDE launches DBT scheme to extend direct monetary support to apprentices
pib.summary: The Ministry announced that NAPS would use Direct Benefit Transfer to send the government’s stipend contribution directly to apprentices’ bank accounts through NSDC. The government contribution was set at 25% of the stipend, subject to a maximum of Rs. 1,500 per month, and more than 12 lakh apprentices had been engaged at the time.

pib.headline: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
pib.summary: The release describes NAPS objectives, including promoting on-the-job training, encouraging establishments to enroll apprentices, and expanding opportunities for MSMEs and underserved regions. It reports around 13.38 lakh apprentices engaged since the scheme began and says the government planned to transfer its stipend contribution directly to apprentices’ bank accounts through DBT.

pib.headline: Shri Dharmendra Pradhan launches DBT in NAPS to strengthen apprenticeship ecosystem in India
pib.summary: The Union Minister launched Direct Benefit Transfer under NAPS and disbursed approximately Rs. 15 crore to one lakh apprentices. The release also states that 25 lakh youth had been engaged as apprentices since NAPS began in 2016, as of 31 July 2023.

pib.headline: Central Apprenticeship Council recommends 36% Increase in Stipend for Youth under National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme and National Apprenticeship Training Scheme
pib.summary: The Central Apprenticeship Council recommended a 36% increase in the stipend range for NAPS and NATS apprentices, from ₹5,000–₹9,000 to ₹6,800–₹12,300. The recommendation also proposed biennial adjustment of stipends based on changes in the Consumer Price Index.

pib.headline: Apprenticeship Reforms and the Central Apprenticeship Council’s Recommendations
pib.summary: The release reports that 8,52,376 apprentices were undergoing training under NAPS-2 as of 30 June 2025, including 1,95,680 women. It also outlines portal upgrades, revised guidelines, strengthened monitoring, financial support for apprenticeship melas, and efforts to expand establishment participation.

pib.headline: Status of Apprentice Scheme
pib.summary: The release states that NAPS-2 had a physical target of 13 lakh apprentices for financial year 2025–26, with 3.99 lakh engaged through July 2025. It also reports 41,95,703 apprentices engaged nationwide from FY 2018–19 through July 2025, of whom 21,47,122 had completed training.

pib.headline: NATIONAL APPRENTICESHIP AND TRAINING SCHEMES
pib.summary: The release explains that NAPS, launched in 2016 and continued as NAPS-2 from 2022–23, is one of the government’s two flagship apprenticeship schemes. It reports that 11.84 lakh apprentices were engaged under NAPS in 2025, alongside 5.23 lakh under NATS.

verdict.name: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
verdict.summary: No CAG audit findings are available for this scheme yet.

scheme.name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)
scheme.description: Rural component of the Swachh Bharat Mission aiming to eliminate open defecation in rural India through construction of individual household toilets (IHHLs) and behaviour change.
scheme.goals: Make all villages, gram panchayats, districts, states Open Defecation Free (ODF) by 2 October 2019. Construct 10 crore toilets. Establish solid and liquid waste management in all villages.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Rural households without toilets; 6 lakh villages across India

pib.headline: India declared ODF on Gandhi Jayanti: 10 crore toilets built in 5 years
pib.summary: PM declares India Open Defecation Free on Gandhi Jayanti 2019. Announces 10.28 crore toilets built, sanitation coverage risen from 38.7% to 100%.

pib.headline: ODF Plus: 5 lakh villages achieve solid and liquid waste management
pib.summary: Jal Shakti Ministry announces 5 lakh villages have achieved ODF Plus status with solid and liquid waste management under SBM-G Phase II.

pib.headline: India Achieves Another Major Sanitation Milestone - 50% Villages Are Now ODF Plus Under Swachh Bharat Mission Grameen Phase II
pib.summary: The press release states that 50% of India’s villages had achieved ODF Plus status under Phase II of the Swachh Bharat Mission Grameen. Nearly 3 lakh villages had declared themselves ODF Plus, supporting the mission’s 2024-25 goals.

pib.headline: Uttar Pradesh Achieves 100% ODF Plus Coverage under Swachh Bharat Mission Grameen
pib.summary: Uttar Pradesh achieved ODF Plus status in all 95,767 villages under Phase II of the Swachh Bharat Mission Grameen. Of these, 81,744 were ODF Plus Aspiring, 10,217 were ODF Plus Rising and 3,806 were ODF Plus Model villages.

pib.headline: Vini Mahajan Inaugurates National Conference on JJM & SBM-G at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
pib.summary: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation inaugurated a national conference on Jal Jeevan Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen in Lucknow. The conference focused on the missions’ progress, sustainability, convergence and achieving Sampoorna Swachhta.

pib.headline: C.R. Patil Holds Review Meeting of North-Eastern States at Guwahati, Assam
pib.summary: A review meeting assessed progress under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen in the North-Eastern states. The release reported that 51% of villages in the region had achieved ODF Plus Model status, with Sikkim reaching 100% coverage.

pib.headline: Parliament Question: Objectives Achieved under Swachh Bharat Mission
pib.summary: The release reported that 5,64,096 of India’s 5,86,788 villages had declared themselves ODF Plus as of 17 March 2025. It also stated that 5,03,585 villages had solid waste management coverage and 5,22,462 had liquid waste management coverage.

pib.headline: ODF Plus Village under Swachh Bharat Mission
pib.summary: The release explained the criteria and verification process for declaring villages ODF Plus under SBM (Gramin). It described the Aspiring, Rising and Model stages, including requirements for solid and liquid waste management, visual cleanliness and third-party verification for Model villages.

pib.headline: Conference on Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen (SBM-G) Progress & Brainstorming on SBM-G Next Phase
pib.summary: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation announced a roundtable conference to review SBM-G progress and develop priorities for its next phase. The release reported over 11.93 crore individual household latrines, 2.62 lakh community sanitary complexes, 4.76 lakh ODF Plus Model villages, more than 950 functional GOBARdhan projects and 124 faecal sludge treatment plants.

cag.finding: Shortfall in achievement of targets was noticed: Individual Household Latrines for 2,14,647 households under Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) in Punjab were yet to be constructed despite availability of funds.
cag.parameter: Individual Household Latrine construction
cag.actual: 2,14,647 households' IHHLs remained unconstructed

cag.finding: Planning and implementation of Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) by Uttarakhand was inadequate: against targets of 546 Community Sanitary Complexes and 4,485 Solid and Liquid Waste Management structures, only 63 and 50 respectively had been constructed up to March 2017.
cag.parameter: Community Sanitary Complexes and Solid and Liquid Waste Management structures
cag.claimed: 546 Community Sanitary Complexes and 4,485 Solid and Liquid Waste Management structures
cag.actual: 63 Community Sanitary Complexes and 50 Solid and Liquid Waste Management structures constructed

cag.finding: The main objective of the rural sanitation programme to make all Ganga river basin villages Open Defecation Free under Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) could not be achieved. Audit also recommended that the reliability of data reported under the SBM (Gramin) Management Information System be ensured through cross-checking with monthly physical and financial reports.
cag.parameter: Open Defecation Free status and rural sanitation monitoring
cag.actual: The objective of making all Ganga river basin villages Open Defecation Free was not achieved

cag.finding: The objectives of Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) were not achieved by 2 October 2019 because all households without toilets were not included in the baseline survey. Consequently, the Department constructed 44,712 IHHLs in excess of the target set in the Project Implementation Plan during 2014-15 to 2019-20.
cag.parameter: Baseline survey coverage and Individual Household Latrine construction
cag.claimed: Target set in the Project Implementation Plan
cag.actual: 44,712 IHHLs constructed in excess of the Project Implementation Plan target

verdict.name: Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)
verdict.summary: Accountability concerns: 1 critical and 3 major findings indicate the scheme is not meeting its stated objectives.

scheme.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
scheme.description: Scheme to issue Soil Health Cards to farmers carrying crop-wise nutrient recommendations based on soil test results, to promote balanced use of fertilisers and improve soil health.
scheme.goals: Issue 14 crore soil health cards to all farmers in 2 cycles of 3 years each. Reduce fertiliser subsidy bill. Improve soil fertility and crop productivity.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: All 14 crore farming households across India

pib.headline: 23 crore Soil Health Cards issued to farmers across India
pib.summary: Agriculture Ministry announces 23 crore soil health cards issued to farmers in two cycles, covering all 14 crore farm holdings across India.

pib.headline: Soil Health Card scheme of Central Govt: A success story
pib.summary: The release says 11.69 crore Soil Health Cards were distributed to farmers during the scheme’s second phase over two years. It also reports that the use of chemical fertilizers declined by 10 percent.

pib.headline: Improving Soil Productivity and Fertility
pib.summary: The release describes the Soil Health Card Scheme’s objective of providing farmers with soil nutrient information and fertilizer recommendations every two years. It highlights the 2019–20 Model Villages pilot, which involved farm-level soil sampling with farmer participation, along with training, demonstrations and farmer campaigns.

pib.headline: Soil health card Scheme Completes 5 years on 19-2-2020; Soil health Cards issued every 2 years to Farmers; Soil health leads to Sustainable Farming
pib.summary: The release reviews the scheme’s five-year implementation and explains that Soil Health Cards provide nutrient-status information and recommendations for improving soil fertility. It reports that 10.74 crore cards were distributed during the first cycle and 11.69 crore during the second cycle.
pib.figureUnit: crore Soil Health Cards in Cycle II

pib.headline: Soil Health Card Day to be Observed Tomorrow; Deteriorating Soil Health Leads to Stagnation in Agricultural Productivity; Soil Health Leads to Sustainable Farming
pib.summary: The release announces Soil Health Card Day and explains that the scheme is intended to issue cards to farmers every two years to address nutrient deficiencies. It emphasizes soil testing as a means to reduce cultivation costs through appropriate fertilizer use and support sustainable farming.
pib.figureUnit: years between Soil Health Card cycles

pib.headline: Soil Health Card Scheme helped India achieve surplus capacity in foodgrain production: Shri Narendra Singh Tomar
pib.summary: At a National Workshop on Soil Health Card Day, the Agriculture Minister said the scheme had contributed to India achieving surplus foodgrain production capacity. The release states that more than 11 crore Soil Health Cards had been issued in two phases and that cards provide soil-health status and crop-specific nutrient recommendations.

pib.headline: SOIL HEALTH CARD SCHEME
pib.summary: The release explains that Soil Health Cards promote balanced fertilizer use and recommend biofertilizers, micronutrients and organic manures. It also reports the establishment of soil-testing laboratories and describes training and demonstrations intended to improve farmer awareness of soil health management.

pib.headline: New Soil Health Card Scheme
pib.summary: The Government introduced technological improvements to the Soil Health Card Scheme, including a revamped portal integrated with geographic information systems so test results can be captured and viewed on maps. The mobile application was enhanced with geolocation, QR-code linking and direct transfer of test results from geo-mapped laboratories, with the new system rolled out from April 2023.

pib.headline: Soil Health Management and Soil Health Card Schemes
pib.summary: The release reports that 23.58 crore Soil Health Cards had been distributed to farmers. It also states that the Soil Health Management and Soil Health Card schemes were merged into the Soil Health & Fertility component of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana.

cag.finding: Implementation of the Soil Health Card Scheme remained ineffective due to inefficient flow of funds, deficient planning for providing financial assistance for recommended nutrients, and non-planning for training and workshops.
cag.parameter: Soil Health Card Scheme implementation

cag.finding: Soil testing laboratories were underutilised, resulting in slow implementation of the Soil Health Cards Scheme; the shortfall in analysing soil samples ranged between 13.49 per cent and 45.92 per cent.
cag.parameter: Soil sample analysis and soil testing laboratory utilisation
cag.actual: Shortfall in analysing soil samples ranged between 13.49 per cent and 45.92 per cent

verdict.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
verdict.summary: 2 major CAG findings indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: Pradhan Mantri Jan Aushadhi Pariyojana (PMJAP)
scheme.description: Scheme to make quality generic medicines available at affordable prices through dedicated retail stores called Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs) across the country.
scheme.goals: Open 10,500 Jan Aushadhi Kendras by March 2025. Offer 2,000+ generic medicines at 50-90% less than branded prices. Save patients Rs 5,000 crore annually.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: All citizens especially poor, elderly, and those with chronic diseases

pib.headline: Jan Aushadhi medicines available at 50-90% less than MRP
pib.summary: Chemicals Ministry announces over 2,000 medicines and 300 surgical devices available at Jan Aushadhi Kendras at 50-90% below branded MRP.

pib.headline: 10,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras operational, saving Rs 20,000 crore to patients
pib.summary: Ministry announces 10,000 Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras operational across India, saving patients Rs 20,000 crore annually on medicines.

pib.headline: 13,822 Jan Aushadhi Kendras have been established across the country; medicines worth Rs. 6,100 crores sold through PMBJP, leading to estimated savings of Rs. 30,000 crores
pib.summary: As of September 30, 2024, a total of 13,822 Jan Aushadhi Kendras had been established nationwide. The release said medicines worth Rs. 6,100 crore had been sold through the scheme over the previous 10 years, generating estimated savings of Rs. 30,000 crore for citizens compared with branded medicines.

pib.headline: Union Minister inaugurates week-long celebrations of Jan Aushadhi Diwas 2025 by flagging off vehicles carrying information about PMBJP
pib.summary: The Union Minister inaugurated the week-long Jan Aushadhi Diwas 2025 celebrations and flagged off a Rath and 10 vehicles to disseminate information about the scheme. The release stated that 15,000 Jan Aushadhi Kendras had been opened by February 28, 2025, and that the government had set a target of 25,000 Kendras by March 31, 2027.

pib.headline: Jan Aushadhi - Virasat Ke Saath: Second day of celebrations for Jan Aushadhi Diwas 2025
pib.summary: The second day of Jan Aushadhi Diwas 2025 featured heritage walks at 25 monuments across the country to spread awareness about affordable generic medicines. More than 500 free health camps, or Jan Arogya Melas, were also organized, particularly for senior citizens.

pib.headline: Jan Aushadhi-Bal Mitra Participation: Third day of celebrations for Jan Aushadhi Diwas 2025
pib.summary: The third day of the celebrations involved Bal Mitra activities in 30 major cities across 30 states to raise awareness among children about quality generic medicines available through Jan Aushadhi Kendras. Nutraceutical products such as Poshan were distributed to participating children.

pib.headline: Jan Aushadhi Diwas celebrated with week-long events; more than 200 new Jan Aushadhi Kendras opened, taking the total to 15,291
pib.summary: The seventh Jan Aushadhi Diwas was observed nationwide under the theme “Jan Aushadhi: Daam Kam, Dawai Uttam,” concluding week-long awareness activities held from March 1 to 7, 2025. The release reported that more than 200 new Kendras had opened during the period, taking the nationwide total to 15,291.

verdict.name: Pradhan Mantri Jan Aushadhi Pariyojana (PMJAP)
verdict.summary: No CAG audit findings are available for this scheme yet.

scheme.name: eNAM (National Agriculture Market)
scheme.description: Pan-India electronic trading portal for agricultural commodities providing a single window service for all APMC related information and services. Enables farmers to get better prices through online competitive bidding.
scheme.goals: Integrate 585 APMCs with eNAM by 2018. Enable 1,000 mandis by 2020. Allow farmers to sell produce from any part of country. Increase farmer income by 20%.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: Farmers, traders, and buyers of agricultural produce across integrated mandis

pib.headline: eNAM: 1.76 crore farmers, 2.26 lakh traders registered; Rs 2.37 lakh crore trade
pib.summary: Agriculture Ministry announces eNAM platform has 1.76 crore farmer registrations, 2.26 lakh traders and trade worth Rs 2.37 lakh crore conducted on the platform.

pib.headline: National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) — One Nation One Market for Agricultural produce
pib.summary: The explainer describes e-NAM as a pan-India electronic trading portal linking Agricultural Produce Market Committee mandis into a unified national market. It highlights transparent online bidding, real-time price discovery, quality assaying and online payments for agricultural produce.
pib.figureUnit: lakh rupees maximum assistance per market

pib.headline: eNAM: Transforming Agricultural Trade into a Seamless Experience
pib.summary: The factsheet reports that e-NAM had integrated 1,389 mandis across 23 States and 4 Union Territories. It also records more than 1.77 crore registered farmers, 2.53 lakh traders and cumulative trade valued at approximately ₹3.19 lakh crore as of the stated reporting periods.

pib.headline: Farmer enrolment on e-NAM platform
pib.summary: The Ministry outlined measures to increase and simplify farmer enrolment on e-NAM, including registration at mandi premises, online portal and mobile-app registration, awareness campaigns and a toll-free helpline. The release reported 1,77,55,957 farmers enrolled across States and Union Territories.

pib.headline: Implementing of National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) Platform
pib.summary: The release states that e-NAM enables online trading of agricultural and horticultural commodities through competitive bidding and transparent price discovery. As of October 31, 2024, 1,389 mandis were integrated, with 1.78 crore farmers, 2.62 lakh traders and more than 4,250 FPOs registered; cumulative trade was reported at ₹3.79 lakh crore.

pib.headline: e-NAM Platform expanded to boost agricultural trade with addition of 10 new commodities and their tradable parameters
pib.summary: The Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare approved tradable parameters for 10 additional commodities, expanding the range of commodities covered by e-NAM. The total number of commodities with formulated tradable parameters consequently reached 231.

pib.headline: Encouraging Farmers to Participate in e-NAM Platform
pib.summary: The release describes online registration, training, helpline support, FPO aggregation and the farm-gate module as measures to encourage small and marginal farmers to use e-NAM. It reported 4,392 FPOs onboarded and tradable parameters finalized for 231 commodities as of February 28, 2025, while also describing plans for e-NAM 2.0.

pib.headline: Registration of FPOs, Farmers and Traders on e-NAM Platform

pib.headline: Agricultural Markets Linked to e-NAM
pib.summary: The release stated that 1,522 mandis had been integrated with the e-NAM portal as of June 30, 2025. It reported trade of 12.03 crore metric tonnes of agricultural commodities and 49.15 crore countable units, including coconut, betel leaf, sweet corn, lemon and bamboo.

pib.headline: Farmers Registered on e-NAM Platform
pib.summary: The release reported that e-NAM had onboarded 1,522 mandis and registered 1,79,41,613 farmers, 2,67,719 traders and 4,518 FPOs as of June 30, 2025. It placed the cumulative value of agricultural produce traded on the platform at ₹4,39,941 crore.

pib.headline: e-NAM Platform Expanded: 09 New Commodities Added to Boost India’s largest digital agri-trade platform
pib.summary: The Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare added nine commodities to e-NAM in response to demand from farmers, traders and other stakeholders. The additions increased the total number of tradable agricultural commodities on the platform to 247.

cag.finding: The Market Board received ₹138.94 crore from the Government of India during 2017-18 to 2021-22 for implementation of three centrally sponsored schemes, including Electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM).

scheme.name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
scheme.description: Scheme for rural electrification focusing on feeder separation of agricultural and domestic supply, strengthening sub-transmission and distribution infrastructure in rural areas.
scheme.goals: Electrify all remaining 18,452 unelectrified villages by May 2018. Provide electricity connections to 2.37 crore BPL rural households. Strengthen rural distribution infrastructure.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 18,452 unelectrified villages; 2.37 crore BPL rural households

pib.headline: PM: Every village in India now electrified — promise fulfilled
pib.summary: PM announces all 18,452 villages electrified under DDUGJY, fulfilling pre-election promise ahead of schedule by bringing electricity to last village Leisang in Manipur.

pib.headline: DDUGJY: 2.63 crore BPL households given electricity connections
pib.summary: Power Ministry announces 2.63 crore Below Poverty Line rural households provided with electricity connections under DDUGJY/Saubhagya schemes.

pib.headline: Year End Review 2020 – Ministry of Power
pib.summary: The release states that DDUGJY had a total outlay of Rs. 75,893 crore, including Rs. 43,033 crore for DDUGJY and Rs. 32,860 crore for the rural electrification component. Projects costing Rs. 44,416 crore had been sanctioned in 33 States and Union Territories, with additional infrastructure sanctioned to support household electrification.

pib.headline: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) for rural electrification works
pib.summary: The release describes DDUGJY’s rural electrification components, including feeder separation, strengthening of sub-transmission and distribution infrastructure, metering, and village electrification. It notes that the scheme was launched in December 2014 for rural electrification works across the country.

pib.headline: Villages electrified under Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
pib.summary: The release says that all villages and all willing households had been electrified by March 31, 2019, as reported by State Governments, through DDUGJY and Saubhagya. It also states that 2.86 crore households were electrified under Saubhagya, including households that became willing later.

pib.headline: Rural Electrification Schemes
pib.summary: The release outlines DDUGJY’s objectives of electrifying un-electrified Census 2011 villages and strengthening rural distribution infrastructure through lines, metering, and feeder segregation. It also reports that 2.86 crore households had been electrified under Saubhagya after additional household electrification was sanctioned.

pib.headline: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY) scheme under Ministry of Power strengthens the electricity distribution system across the country
pib.summary: The release reports that DDUGJY strengthened electricity distribution through new and augmented substations, feeder separation, transformers, transmission lines, and village electrification. It states that 18,374 villages were electrified under the scheme.

pib.headline: STATUS OF DDUGJY - A total of 18,374 villages were electrified under the scheme
pib.summary: The release states that all inhabited un-electrified Census 2011 villages had been electrified by April 28, 2018 under DDUGJY. It reports 18,374 villages electrified nationwide and says the scheme stood closed as of March 31, 2022.

pib.headline: Nearly 88,000 households of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups to be provided electricity under PM JANMAN
pib.summary: The release reports that 18,374 villages were electrified under the rural electrification programme, including 2,763 villages electrified through renewable resources. It also states that 2.86 crore households were electrified under Saubhagya.

pib.headline: DDUGJY
pib.summary: The release explains DDUGJY’s components and reports that Tamil Nadu’s sanctioned works included substations, feeder separation, distribution lines, meters, and household connections. It states that all physical works in Tamil Nadu were completed by December 31, 2020 and that the scheme stands closed.

pib.headline: BENEFICIARIES UNDER DDUGJY
pib.summary: The release describes DDUGJY’s provision of electricity connections to BPL households and other rural households, including households left out under Saubhagya. It provides State-wise and year-wise household electrification details and notes that the scheme was closed on March 31, 2022.

cag.finding: CAG found government's claim of electrifying all 18,452 villages used a definition requiring only 10% of households to have power. Actual household electrification was 77% at the time of the ODF declaration. 3.3 crore households in "electrified" villages had no connection.
cag.parameter: Village electrification vs household access
cag.actual: Only 10% households needed for "electrified" status

cag.finding: CAG survey in 21 states found rural households received average of 12.5 hours electricity per day despite target of 24 hours. In UP, Bihar and Jharkhand, average supply was 6-8 hours. Rs 2,300 crore of infrastructure was stranded due to state DISCOM non-payment.
cag.parameter: Supply quality and hours in rural areas
cag.actual: 12.5 hours average supply

cag.finding: Electrification of 819 (10 per cent) out of 7,925 villages taken up under DDUGJY was not completed as of March 2020. Further, 68,417 (32 per cent) out of 2,15,605 DDUGJY connections could not be provided.
cag.parameter: Village and household electrification
cag.actual: 819 villages and 68,417 connections remained incomplete/unprovided

cag.finding: Out of 2,339 unelectrified villages sanctioned under the scheme, APDCL electrified only 996 villages; the remaining 1,343 villages were found to be partially electrified while executing the scheme works.
cag.parameter: Village electrification
cag.actual: 996 villages electrified; 1,343 villages partially electrified

cag.finding: Infructuous expenditure of ₹1.18 crore was incurred on installations of M&P boxes under DDUGJY.
cag.parameter: Project execution and expenditure
cag.actual: ₹1.18 crore of infructuous expenditure

cag.finding: The works for all 21 DDUGJY projects were awarded with delays ranging between 306 and 657 days, with an average delay of 470 days.
cag.parameter: Project award and implementation delay
cag.actual: 306–657 days of delay, averaging 470 days

cag.finding: The audit identified deficiencies in DDUGJY implementation, including execution of work not conforming to Detailed Project Reports, failure to impose liquidated damages, delays in execution of projects, failure to realise additional grant, discrepancies in beneficiary data and closure reports, and deficiencies in project monitoring.
cag.parameter: Project execution, financial management and monitoring
cag.actual: Deficiencies and control failures identified across DDUGJY projects

cag.finding: The objective of separating agriculture and non-agriculture feeders under DDUGJY was not achieved. The audit also reported avoidable expenditure due to execution of unnecessary items and double payment for installation of meters at consumers' premises.
cag.parameter: Feeder separation and project expenditure
cag.actual: Feeder-separation objective not achieved; unnecessary works and double meter payments identified

verdict.name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
verdict.summary: Severe accountability failure: 5 critical findings by CAG. Significant gap between stated goals and ground reality.

scheme.name: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
scheme.description: Mission to develop a national digital health ecosystem that supports universal health coverage. Creates a Health ID (ABHA) for every citizen linking all health records digitally.
scheme.goals: Create health IDs for 100 crore citizens. Digitize health records of all citizens. Create national registries of doctors and health facilities. Enable paperless health ecosystem.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: All 140 crore citizens of India

pib.headline: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission: 22 crore ABHA IDs created in one year
pib.summary: Health Ministry marks first anniversary of ABDM with 22 crore Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) IDs created. 1.2 lakh health facilities registered.

pib.headline: Update on Digital Healthcare Mechanism
pib.summary: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission supports integration of India's digital health infrastructure through applications such as the ABHA app and Aarogya Setu. The release also describes assisted and offline ABHA creation, open standards, the ABDM sandbox, and initiatives to accelerate digital-health adoption.

pib.headline: National Digital Health Ecosystem
pib.summary: The release states that ABDM aims to create an interoperable digital-health platform and longitudinal electronic health records for citizens. It highlights the Union Health Ministry's holistic approach to protecting the digital-health system from critical security threats and notes the role of the Health Data Management Policy in safeguarding privacy and data protection.

pib.headline: Update on Digital Healthcare Platforms: Electronic Health Record Standards under Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission aim to facilitate interoperability of healthcare information
pib.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has notified Electronic Health Record standards to promote interoperability across healthcare information systems. The National Health Authority has also issued privacy, data-management, authentication, and sandbox-related guidelines for applications integrated with the ABDM ecosystem.

pib.headline: Update on Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission: More than 52.5 Crore ABHA IDs created
pib.summary: More than 52.5 crore Ayushman Bharat Health Account numbers had been created under ABDM. The release explains that ABHA is a voluntary 14-digit health identifier intended to support interoperable health data and longitudinal electronic health records.

pib.headline: Explainer on Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts (ABHA)
pib.summary: ABHA is described as an integral component of ABDM and a 14-digit unique number that enables digital access to and sharing of health records. The explainer says individuals can enroll voluntarily and free of cost to participate in the ABDM digital-health ecosystem.

pib.headline: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission marks a Transformative Three-Year Journey towards enabling Digital Health
pib.summary: ABDM completed three years since its launch, using digital public infrastructure to promote interoperable, secure, and citizen-centric healthcare. The release reports that more than 67 crore ABHA accounts had been created and outlines key components including the ABHA, healthcare professional, and health facility registries.

pib.headline: Update on Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
pib.summary: As of November 27, 2024, more than 68.97 crore ABHAs had been created, 3.49 lakh health facilities registered on the Health Facility Registry, 5.23 lakh healthcare professionals registered on the Healthcare Professional Registry, and 45.37 crore health records linked with ABHA. The release also reports progress on microsites, Scan and Share, Scan and Pay, and model ABDM facilities.

pib.headline: Update on Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
pib.summary: As of December 10, 2024, more than 71.16 crore ABHAs had been created, with over 3.54 lakh health facilities and 5.37 lakh healthcare professionals registered in the relevant ABDM registries. More than 45.99 crore health records had also been linked with ABHA, while participation in ABDM remained voluntary.

verdict.name: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)
verdict.summary: No CAG audit findings are available for this scheme yet.

scheme.name: Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission

pib.summary: Rural Development Ministry announces 217 Rurban clusters sanctioned across 27 states under Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission.

pib.headline: Aibawk cluster in the Aizawl, Mizoram becomes the first cluster to be completed under the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission
pib.summary: The Aibawk Rurban cluster in Mizoram became the first cluster completed under the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission. It completed all planned projects, including improvements to roads, footpaths, drainage, water supply, market access, livelihoods, tourism and social infrastructure.

scheme.goals: Provide free food grain to 80 crore NFSA beneficiaries during COVID and economic distress. Prevent hunger and starvation. Total expenditure exceeded Rs 3.91 lakh crore.
scheme.targetBeneficiaries: 80 crore National Food Security Act beneficiaries

pib.headline: PM launches Rs 1.70 lakh crore PMGKAY relief package for COVID
pib.summary: PM announces Rs 1.70 lakh crore COVID relief under PMGKAY including free 5 kg grain and 1 kg pulses to 80 crore for 3 months.

pib.headline: PMGKAY extended till December 2023; 80 crore beneficiaries to get free grain
pib.summary: PM announces PMGKAY extended for one more year covering 80 crore NFSA beneficiaries with 5 kg free grain per month. Total expenditure to reach Rs 3.91 lakh crore.

pib.headline: Free Foodgrains for 81.35 crore beneficiaries for five years: Cabinet Decision
pib.summary: The Cabinet approved free food grains under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana for about 81.35 crore beneficiaries for five years beginning January 1, 2024. The initiative covers rice, wheat and coarse grains, with an estimated food subsidy of Rs. 11.80 lakh crore over the five-year period.

pib.headline: Cabinet approves continuation of supply of free Fortified Rice under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) and other welfare schemes from July, 2024 to December, 2028
pib.summary: The Union Cabinet approved continuation of the universal supply of fortified rice under PMGKAY and other government welfare schemes from July 2024 through December 2028. The initiative is fully funded by the Government of India and aims to address anaemia and micronutrient deficiencies.

pib.headline: Year-End Review of Department of Food and Public Distribution–2024
pib.summary: The 2024 review states that free food grain distribution under PMGKAY was extended for five years from January 1, 2024, following the initial one-year period that began in 2023. It reports that approximately 80.67 crore people were receiving food grains free of cost against intended coverage of 81.35 crore persons.

cag.finding: After implementation of PMGKAY, 31.05 lakh NFSA-PHH beneficiaries with one to three members received no additional rice compared with their pre-PMGKAY entitlement. Separate stock and distribution registers for PMGKAY were not maintained in 88 per cent of the test-checked Fair Price Shops.

cag.claimed: Five kg of additional rice per person per month under PMGKAY

verdict.name: PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)

scheme.name: Sagarmala Programme
scheme.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
scheme.description: Programme for port-led development to reduce logistics cost for EXIM and domestic trade with minimal infrastructure investment through optimum utilization of waterways.
scheme.goals: Implement 415 projects worth Rs 8 lakh crore by 2035. Reduce logistics cost from 14% to 8% of GDP. Create 1 crore new jobs.

pib.headline: Sagarmala: 802 projects worth Rs 5.48 lakh crore under implementation
pib.summary: Ports Ministry announces 802 Sagarmala projects worth Rs 5.48 lakh crore under various stages of implementation. 202 projects completed.

pib.headline: Growth of Indian Maritime Sector
pib.summary: The Government says the Sagarmala Programme includes projects for port modernization, RoRo/RoPax and tourism jetties, port connectivity, fishing harbours, and skill development. A total of 839 projects valued at approximately ₹5.8 lakh crore were identified for implementation, of which 241 projects worth about ₹1.22 lakh crore had been completed.

pib.headline: Sagarmala Projects
pib.summary: The Ministry provided details of Sagarmala-funded projects and financial assistance to states and Union Territories, including port infrastructure, coastal berths, road and rail connectivity, fishing harbours, and cruise terminals. Under the scheme, 130 projects with a total project cost of ₹9,580 crore were listed, with ₹3,714 crore sanctioned.

pib.headline: Sagarmala Projects: Transforming Andhra Pradesh with more than Rs.7000 Crore Investment
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that 29 new proposals from Andhra Pradesh, worth approximately ₹3,300 crore, had been received under the Sagarmala Programme. It also stated that 13 projects valued at about ₹2,500 crore were receiving financial assistance, while projects undertaken by Visakhapatnam Port Authority and IWAI represented combined investment of ₹4,600 crore.

pib.headline: SAGARMALA SCHEME
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that 119 projects costing ₹9,407 crore had been undertaken for partial funding under the Sagarmala Scheme. Of these, 72 projects had been completed, while eight projects worth ₹273 crore were receiving assistance in Kerala.

pib.headline: Sagarmala Programme in Tamilnadu
pib.summary: The Ministry provided a state-wise update on Sagarmala-funded projects in Tamil Nadu, covering port infrastructure, coastal berths, fishing harbours, skill development, and coastal community development. The listed projects included completed and under-implementation works with details of project costs, sanctioned funds, and funds released.

cag.finding: Under the Sagarmala Programme, Andhra Pradesh proposed nine jetty projects and committed to bear 50 per cent of the project cost. Only one project, the Bhavani Island jetty, was approved; work was halted after execution of works worth ₹4.79 crore because the State did not release its ₹5 crore share. Of the remaining eight projects, revised DPRs were submitted for only three, while no decision was taken on the other five proposals.

cag.actual: 1 project approved; work halted after ₹4.79 crore of works, with 8 remaining proposals not completed

verdict.summary: 1 major CAG finding indicate gaps between PIB claims and actual implementation.

scheme.name: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)

scheme.description: Maternity benefit programme providing cash incentive of Rs 5,000 to pregnant and lactating mothers for the first live birth to partly compensate for wage loss and improve health seeking behaviour.

pib.headline: PMMVY: Rs 10,000 crore disbursed to 3.04 crore beneficiaries since 2017
pib.summary: Women & Child Ministry announces Rs 10,000 crore cash transferred to 3.04 crore pregnant and lactating mothers under PMMVY since inception.

pib.headline: National Event on Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) held in Mumbai; new PMMVY portal launched and direct benefit cash transfer released to 8,14,612 beneficiaries
pib.summary: A national PMMVY event was held in Mumbai, where a comprehensive user manual and the new PMMVYsoft MIS portal were launched. Direct benefit cash transfers totaling Rs 321.57 crore were released to 8,14,612 beneficiaries.

pib.headline: Year End Review-2023: Ministry of Women and Child Development
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that more than 64,000 POSHAN Abhiyaan and PMMVY beneficiaries shared their experiences during the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra, with more than 92,000 on-the-spot registrations conducted under various Ministry schemes. The review also highlighted the additional Rs 6,000 benefit for a second girl child and the development of the PMMVY portal and mobile app.

pib.headline: Under PMMVY, maternity benefits are provided to eligible women; husband’s Aadhaar is not mandatory
pib.summary: The Ministry stated that PMMVY maternity benefits are available to eligible women aged 18 years and 7 months to 55 years. It also clarified that a husband’s Aadhaar is not mandatory for receiving benefits under the Mission Shakti version of PMMVY, supported by the PMMVYSoft system.

pib.headline: Over 53.76 Lakh Beneficiaries Covered Under PMMVY Scheme in FY 2023-24
pib.summary: The Ministry reported that 53,76,728 beneficiaries were covered under PMMVY during financial year 2023-24. The release also described the Rs 5,000 benefit for the first child and the Rs 6,000 benefit for a second child when the second child is a girl.

pib.headline: Special Registration Drive for Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana Extended Till August 15, 2025; 4.05 Cr Women Receive Benefits Since Inception
pib.summary: The Ministry extended the special door-to-door registration and awareness drive for PMMVY until August 15, 2025. It reported that more than 4.05 crore beneficiaries had received at least one maternity-benefit instalment, totaling Rs 19,028 crore, through direct benefit transfer up to July 31, 2025.

pib.headline: PMKSY: 76.03 lakh hectares additional land brought under irrigation
